3301	fn chain_extend_command(
3302	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
3303	    id: &str,
3304	    step_goal: String,
3305	    insert_at: Option<u32>,

3311	        return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
3312	            "cannot extend completed chain at end",

3322	    let insert = insert_at
3323	        .map(|value| value.saturating_sub(1) as usize)
3324	        .unwrap_or(chain.steps.len())

298	  deadreckon resume latest --from-turn 2
299	  deadreckon attach latest
300	
301	Resume reconstructs history from traces, skips partial trailing records, and continues the run.";

99	                });

106	struct JsonlTail {
107	    path: PathBuf,
108	    offset: u64,
109	    partial: String,
110	}
111	
112	impl JsonlTail {
113	    fn new(path: PathBuf) -> Self {
114	        Self {
115	            path,
116	            offset: 0,
117	            partial: String::new(),
118	        }
119	    }
120	
121	    fn read_new(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<Vec<RunEvent>> {
122	        let Some(mut file) = self.open_at_offset()? else {
123	            return Ok(Vec::new());
124	        };
125	        let mut raw = String::new();
126	        file.read_to_string(&mut raw)?;
127	        self.offset = file.stream_position()?;
128	        if raw.is_empty() {
129	            return Ok(Vec::new());
130	        }
131	        let mut buffer = String::new();
132	        std::mem::swap(&mut buffer, &mut self.partial);
133	        buffer.push_str(&raw);
134	        let complete = buffer.ends_with('\n');
135	        let mut lines = buffer.lines().map(str::to_string).collect::<Vec<_>>();
136	        if !complete {
137	            self.partial = lines.pop().unwrap_or_default();
138	        }
139	        Ok(lines
140	            .into_iter()
141	            .filter(|line| !line.trim().is_empty())
142	            .filter_map(|line| serde_json::from_str::<RunEvent>(&line).ok())
143	            .collect())
144	    }
145	
146	    fn skip_to_end(&mut self) {
147	        self.offset = fs::metadata(&self.path)
148	            .map(|metadata| metadata.len())
149	            .unwrap_or(0);
150	        self.partial.clear();
151	    }
152	
153	    fn open_at_offset(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<Option<fs::File>> {
154	        if !self.path.exists() {
155	            self.offset = 0;
156	            self.partial.clear();
157	            return Ok(None);
158	        }
159	        let metadata = fs::metadata(&self.path)?;
160	        if metadata.len() < self.offset {
161	            self.offset = 0;
162	            self.partial.clear();
163	        }
164	        let mut file = fs::File::open(&self.path)?;
165	        file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(self.offset))?;
166	        Ok(Some(file))
167	    }
168	}

103	fn error_hint(err: &CliError) -> Option<&'static str> {
104	    match err {
105	        CliError::Provider(deadreckon_providers::ProviderError::MissingCredential(_))
106	        | CliError::Provider(deadreckon_providers::ProviderError::NoRoute(_)) => Some(
107	            "run `deadreckon init` or `deadreckon config set providers.anthropic.api_key <KEY>`",
108	        ),
109	        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(message))
110	            if message.contains("max spend above $50") =>
111	        {
112	            Some("rerun with `--i-know-its-a-lot` or lower `--max-spend`")
113	        }
114	        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::NotFound(_)) => {
115	            Some("run `deadreckon list` to find valid run ids or config keys")
116	        }
117	        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::LockHeld { .. }) => Some(
118	            "run `deadreckon list`, then `deadreckon attach <run-id>` or `deadreckon kill <run-id>`",
119	        ),

125	        CliError::Json(_) => Some("inspect the referenced JSON file for invalid syntax"),
126	        CliError::Core(_) | CliError::Provider(_) => None,
127	    }

136	fn ui_enabled(stream: UiStream) -> bool {

138	        return false;
139	    }
140	    if std::env::var("TERM").is_ok_and(|term| term == "dumb") {
141	        return false;
142	    }
143	    match stream {
144	        UiStream::Stdout => io::stdout().is_terminal(),
145	        UiStream::Stderr => io::stderr().is_terminal(),
146	    }
147	}

126	const DONE_HELP: &str = "\
127	Lifecycle:
128	  deadreckon def-done \"builds, opens in a browser, and has no console errors\"
129	  deadreckon run \"finish the app\"
130	
131	Common actions:
132	  deadreckon def-done \"plain-English definition of done\"
133	  deadreckon def-done add \"one more thing that must be true\"
134	  deadreckon def-done add browser
135	  deadreckon def-done check
136	  deadreckon def-done show
137	
138	What it means:
139	  Write done criteria in English. deadreckon compiles them into checks for dr-gate.
140	  `deadreckon run` and `deadreckon chain run` prompt for this when criteria are missing.";
141	
142	const ACCEPTANCE_HELP: &str = "\
143	Advanced compatibility command. Most users should use `deadreckon def-done`.
144	
145	Subcommands:
146	  deadreckon acceptance setup
147	  deadreckon acceptance setup \"build, load in a browser, and show no console errors\"
148	  deadreckon acceptance add browser
149	  deadreckon acceptance add \"users can add artwork and browse the gallery\"
150	  deadreckon acceptance init --preset auto
151	  deadreckon acceptance draft \"generate acceptance for this app\"
152	  deadreckon acceptance refine \"also require websocket reconnect tests\"
153	  deadreckon acceptance explain
154	  deadreckon acceptance check
155	
156	Lifecycle:
157	  Write criteria in English; deadreckon compiles them to `.deadreckon/acceptance.yaml`.
158	  `deadreckon run` automatically uses it, or pass `--acceptance <path>`.
159	  `dr-gate` remains the pass/fail authority at completion.
160	
161	Packs:
162	  auto, basic, build, test, rust, node, static-site, browser, playwright, vite, nextjs, python";

164	pub(crate) const CHAIN_HELP: &str = "\
165	Chain subcommands:
166	  deadreckon chain plan \"large goal\" --n 4
167	  deadreckon chain \"step one\" \"step two\" --yes
168	  deadreckon chain run latest
169	  deadreckon chain attach latest
170	  deadreckon chain status latest
171	  deadreckon chain show latest --why-failed

173	  deadreckon chain resume latest
174	  deadreckon chain kill latest
175	  deadreckon chain undo latest --step 2

1006	fn set_provider_model(root: &mut toml::Value, provider: &str, model: &str) {
1007	    if !root.is_table() {
1008	        *root = toml::Value::Table(Default::default());
1009	    }
1010	    let Some(root_table) = root.as_table_mut() else {
1011	        return;
1012	    };
1013	    let providers = root_table
1014	        .entry("providers".to_string())
1015	        .or_insert_with(|| toml::Value::Table(Default::default()));
1016	    if !providers.is_table() {
1017	        *providers = toml::Value::Table(Default::default());
1018	    }
1019	    let Some(providers_table) = providers.as_table_mut() else {
1020	        return;
1021	    };
1022	    let provider_entry = providers_table
1023	        .entry(provider.to_string())
1024	        .or_insert_with(|| toml::Value::Table(Default::default()));
1025	    if !provider_entry.is_table() {
1026	        *provider_entry = toml::Value::Table(Default::default());
1027	    }
1028	    if let Some(provider_table) = provider_entry.as_table_mut() {
1029	        provider_table.insert("model".to_string(), toml::Value::String(model.to_string()));
1030	    }
1031	}

18	    NoRoute(String),

20	    Http { provider: String, detail: String },

27	impl ProviderError {
28	    /// Transient — the operation may succeed on a retry.
29	    pub fn is_retryable(&self) -> bool {
30	        match self {
31	            ProviderError::Io { source, .. } => is_retryable_io_kind(source.kind()),
32	            ProviderError::Toml { .. } => false,
33	            ProviderError::MissingCredential(_) => false,
34	            ProviderError::NoRoute(_) => false,
35	            ProviderError::Http { .. } => false,
36	            ProviderError::Cli { .. } => false,
37	            ProviderError::InvalidConfig(_) => false,
38	        }
39	    }
40	
41	    /// Unrecoverable — the watchdog should escalate, not retry.
42	    pub fn is_fatal(&self) -> bool {
43	        match self {
44	            ProviderError::Io { source, .. } => !is_retryable_io_kind(source.kind()),
45	            ProviderError::Toml { .. } => true,
46	            ProviderError::MissingCredential(_) => true,
47	            ProviderError::NoRoute(_) => true,
48	            ProviderError::Http { .. } => true,
49	            ProviderError::Cli { .. } => true,
50	            ProviderError::InvalidConfig(_) => true,
51	        }
52	    }
53	}
54	
55	fn is_retryable_io_kind(kind: std::io::ErrorKind) -> bool {
56	    matches!(
57	        kind,
58	        std::io::ErrorKind::Interrupted
59	            | std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock
60	            | std::io::ErrorKind::TimedOut
61	            | std::io::ErrorKind::ConnectionReset
62	            | std::io::ErrorKind::ConnectionAborted
63	            | std::io::ErrorKind::BrokenPipe
64	    )
65	}

182	pub fn create_run(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, options: RunOptions) -> Result<PipelineState> {
183	    let scope = workspace_scope(&options.cwd)?;
184	    let task_key = task_key(&options.goal);
185	    let run_id = options
186	        .run_id
187	        .unwrap_or_else(|| Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string());
188	    let run_root = paths.run_root(&scope, &run_id);
189	    let codebase = options.codebase.unwrap_or_else(CodebaseRecord::fresh);
190	    let working_dir = working_dir_for_codebase(&run_root, &codebase);
191	    fs::create_dir_all(&working_dir).with_path(&working_dir)?;
192	    fs::create_dir_all(run_root.join("snapshots")).with_path(run_root.join("snapshots"))?;
193	    let gate_dir = run_root.join("gate");
194	    fs::create_dir_all(&gate_dir).with_path(&gate_dir)?;
195	    fs::write(gate_dir.join("nonce"), Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string())
196	        .with_path(gate_dir.join("nonce"))?;
197	
198	    // AS-BUILT §3: the binary owns deterministic paths while the skill stays a
199	    // markdown subprocess boundary under the source tree.
200	    let skill_path = PathBuf::from(SOURCE_ROOT)
201	        .join("skills")
202	        .join(&options.skill_name)
203	        .join("SKILL.md");
204	    let now = Utc::now();
205	    let mut state = PipelineState {
206	        version: STATE_VERSION,
207	        goal: options.goal,
208	        task_key,
209	        run_id,
210	        scope,
211	        status: RunStatus::Pending,
212	        current_phase_id: PhaseId(0),
213	        started_at: now,
214	        updated_at: now,
215	        cwd: options.cwd,
216	        run_root,
217	        working_dir,
218	        skill_name: options.skill_name,
219	        skill_path,
220	        sandbox: options.sandbox,
221	        provider: options.provider,
222	        max_spend_usd: options.max_spend_usd,
223	        max_wall_seconds: options.max_wall_seconds,
224	        total_spend_usd: 0.0,
225	        total_wall_seconds: 0.0,
226	        turn: 0,
227	        pause_reason: None,
228	        failure_reason: None,
229	        child_pids: Vec::new(),
230	        killed_at: None,
231	        promoted_library_dir: None,
232	        phases: default_phases(now),

234	    state.set_phase_status(PhaseId(0), PhaseStatus::Planned)?;

237	    ensure_docs_started(&state)?;

239	    Ok(state)

315	pub fn find_run_state_path(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, run_id: &str) -> Result<PathBuf> {
316	    let run_id = run_id.trim();
317	    if run_id.is_empty() {
318	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
319	            "run id prefix cannot be empty".to_string(),
320	        ));
321	    }
322	    let root = paths.runstate_dir();
323	    if !root.exists() {
324	        return Err(DeadreckonError::NotFound(format!("run {run_id}")));
325	    }
326	    let mut prefix_matches = Vec::new();
327	    for entry in WalkDir::new(&root)
328	        .into_iter()
329	        .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
330	    {
331	        if !entry.file_type().is_file() || entry.file_name() != "state.json" {
332	            continue;
333	        }
334	        let candidate = entry.path();
335	        let Some(candidate_run_id) = candidate
336	            .parent()
337	            .and_then(Path::file_name)
338	            .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
339	        else {
340	            continue;
341	        };
342	        if candidate_run_id == run_id {
343	            return Ok(candidate.to_path_buf());
344	        }
345	        if candidate_run_id.starts_with(run_id) {
346	            prefix_matches.push((candidate_run_id.to_string(), candidate.to_path_buf()));
347	        }
348	    }
349	    match prefix_matches.len() {
350	        1 => Ok(prefix_matches.remove(0).1),
351	        0 => Err(DeadreckonError::NotFound(format!("run {run_id}"))),
352	        _ => {
353	            let matches = prefix_matches
354	                .into_iter()
355	                .map(|(id, _)| id)
356	                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
357	                .join(", ");
358	            Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
359	                "ambiguous run id prefix {run_id}; matches {matches}"
360	            )))
361	        }

365	pub fn load_run(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, run_id: &str) -> Result<PipelineState> {
366	    let path = find_run_state_path(paths, run_id)?;
367	    load_state(&path)

369	
370	pub fn list_runs(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, scope_filter: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<RunListEntry>> {
371	    let root = paths.runstate_dir();
372	    if !root.exists() {
373	        return Ok(Vec::new());
374	    }
375	    let mut runs = Vec::new();
376	    for entry in WalkDir::new(&root)
377	        .max_depth(4)
378	        .into_iter()
379	        .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
380	    {
381	        if !entry.file_type().is_file() || entry.file_name() != "state.json" {
382	            continue;
383	        }
384	        let state = load_state(entry.path())?;
385	        if scope_filter.is_some_and(|scope| scope != state.scope) {
386	            continue;
387	        }
388	        runs.push(RunListEntry {
389	            run_id: state.run_id,
390	            scope: state.scope,
391	            goal: state.goal,
392	            status: state.status,
393	            updated_at: state.updated_at,
394	            state_path: entry.path().to_path_buf(),
395	        });
396	    }
397	    runs.sort_by(|left, right| right.updated_at.cmp(&left.updated_at));
398	    Ok(runs)
399	}

401	pub(crate) fn atomic_write_json<T: Serialize>(path: &Path, value: &T) -> Result<()> {
402	    let parent = path.parent().ok_or_else(|| {
403	        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("path has no parent: {}", path.display()))
404	    })?;
405	    fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
406	    let mut temp = NamedTempFile::new_in(parent).with_path(parent)?;
407	    serde_json::to_writer_pretty(&mut temp, value).with_json_path(path)?;
408	    temp.write_all(b"\n").with_path(path)?;
409	    temp.as_file_mut().sync_all().with_path(path)?;
410	    persist_temp(temp, path)
411	}
412	
413	fn persist_temp(temp: NamedTempFile, path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
414	    match temp.persist(path) {
415	        Ok(_) => Ok(()),
416	        Err(err) => Err(DeadreckonError::Io {
417	            path: path.to_path_buf(),
418	            source: err.error,
419	        }),
420	    }
421	}
422	
423	pub fn append_json_line<T: Serialize>(path: &Path, value: &T) -> Result<()> {
424	    let parent = path.parent().ok_or_else(|| {
425	        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("path has no parent: {}", path.display()))
426	    })?;
427	    fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
428	    let mut file = File::options()
429	        .create(true)
430	        .append(true)
431	        .open(path)
432	        .with_path(path)?;
433	    serde_json::to_writer(&mut file, value).with_json_path(path)?;
434	    file.write_all(b"\n").with_path(path)?;
435	    file.sync_all().with_path(path)
436	}

959	impl From<CliDocKind> for DocKind {
960	    fn from(value: CliDocKind) -> Self {
961	        match value {
962	            CliDocKind::Narrative => DocKind::Narrative,
963	            CliDocKind::AsBuilt => DocKind::AsBuilt,
964	            CliDocKind::Decisions => DocKind::Decisions,
965	            CliDocKind::Delta => DocKind::Delta,
966	        }
967	    }

10	pub fn read_config(path: &Path) -> Result<ProviderConfigFile> {
11	    match std::fs::read_to_string(path) {
12	        Ok(raw) => {
13	            let mut config: ProviderConfigFile =
14	                toml::from_str(&raw).map_err(|source| ProviderError::Toml {
15	                    path: path.display().to_string(),
16	                    source,
17	                })?;
18	            if config.default_provider.is_none() {
19	                config.default_provider = defaults_provider(&raw);
20	            }
21	            Ok(config)
22	        }
23	        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(ProviderConfigFile {
24	            default_provider: None,
25	            fallback: None,
26	            providers: BTreeMap::new(),
27	        }),
28	        Err(source) => Err(ProviderError::Io {
29	            path: path.display().to_string(),
30	            source,
31	        }),
32	    }
33	}

35	fn defaults_provider(raw: &str) -> Option<String> {
36	    let root: toml::Value = toml::from_str(raw).ok()?;
37	    root.as_table()?
38	        .get("defaults")?
39	        .as_table()?
40	        .get("provider")?
41	        .as_str()
42	        .map(ToString::to_string)
43	}

50	pub(crate) fn provider_entries_from_registry(
51	    registry: &ProviderRegistry,
52	) -> BTreeMap<String, ProviderEntry> {
53	    registry
54	        .iter()
55	        .map(|descriptor| {
56	            (
57	                descriptor.id.clone(),
58	                provider_entry_from_descriptor(descriptor),
59	            )
60	        })
61	        .collect()
62	}
63	
64	pub(crate) fn provider_entry_from_descriptor(descriptor: &ProviderDescriptor) -> ProviderEntry {
65	    let default_model = if descriptor.kind == DescriptorKind::Cli {
66	        None
67	    } else if descriptor.id == "openai-compatible" {
68	        env::var("OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_MODEL")
69	            .ok()
70	            .or_else(|| descriptor.default_model.clone())
71	    } else {
72	        descriptor.default_model.clone()
73	    };
74	    let default_endpoint = if descriptor.id == "openai-compatible" {
75	        env::var("OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL")
76	            .ok()
77	            .or_else(|| descriptor.default_endpoint.clone())
78	    } else {
79	        descriptor.default_endpoint.clone()
80	    };
81	    let default_model_pricing = default_model
82	        .as_deref()
83	        .and_then(|model| {
84	            descriptor
85	                .model_catalog
86	                .iter()
87	                .find(|entry| entry.id == model)
88	        })
89	        .or_else(|| descriptor.model_catalog.first());
90	    ProviderEntry {
91	        kind: Some(kind_from_name(&descriptor.id)),
92	        api_key: None,
93	        api_key_env: descriptor.auth.env_var.clone(),
94	        base_url: default_endpoint,
95	        model: default_model,
96	        input_cost_per_million: default_model_pricing.and_then(|entry| entry.input_per_million),
97	        output_cost_per_million: default_model_pricing.and_then(|entry| entry.output_per_million),
98	        binary: descriptor.default_binary.clone(),
99	        extra_args: Vec::new(),
100	    }
101	}
102	
103	pub(crate) fn merge_provider_entry(base: &mut ProviderEntry, entry: ProviderEntry) {
104	    if entry.kind.is_some() {
105	        base.kind = entry.kind;
106	    }
107	    if entry.api_key.is_some() {
108	        base.api_key = entry.api_key;
109	    }
110	    if entry.api_key_env.is_some() {
111	        base.api_key_env = entry.api_key_env;
112	    }
113	    if entry.base_url.is_some() {
114	        base.base_url = entry.base_url;
115	    }
116	    if entry.model.is_some() {
117	        base.model = entry.model;
118	    }
119	    if entry.input_cost_per_million.is_some() {
120	        base.input_cost_per_million = entry.input_cost_per_million;
121	    }
122	    if entry.output_cost_per_million.is_some() {
123	        base.output_cost_per_million = entry.output_cost_per_million;
124	    }
125	    if entry.binary.is_some() {
126	        base.binary = entry.binary;
127	    }
128	    if !entry.extra_args.is_empty() {
129	        base.extra_args = entry.extra_args;
130	    }
131	}
132	
133	pub(crate) fn kind_from_name(name: &str) -> ProviderKind {
134	    match name {
135	        "anthropic" => ProviderKind::Anthropic,
136	        "openai" => ProviderKind::OpenAi,
137	        "openai-compatible" | "openrouter" | "llama-cpp" => ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible,
138	        "cli:claude-code" | "cli-claude-code" => ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode,
139	        "cli:codex" | "cli-codex" => ProviderKind::CliCodex,
140	        "smoke" => ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke,
141	        _ => ProviderKind::Generic(name.to_string()),
142	    }
143	}

259	    pub fn with_overrides(home: &Path) -> Result<Self> {
260	        let mut registry = Self::builtin()?;
261	        let overrides_dir = home.join("providers.d");
262	        let mut paths = match fs::read_dir(&overrides_dir) {
263	            Ok(entries) => entries
264	                .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
265	                .map(|entry| entry.path())
266	                .filter(|path| path.extension().and_then(|ext| ext.to_str()) == Some("toml"))
267	                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
268	            Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(registry),
269	            Err(source) => {
270	                return Err(ProviderError::Io {
271	                    path: overrides_dir.display().to_string(),
272	                    source,
273	                });
274	            }
275	        };
276	        paths.sort();
277	        for path in paths {
278	            registry.load_override(&path)?;
279	        }
280	        Ok(registry)
281	    }

303	    fn load_override(&mut self, path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
304	        let raw = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|source| ProviderError::Io {
305	            path: path.display().to_string(),
306	            source,
307	        })?;
308	        let mut override_value = parse_toml_value(&raw, path)?;
309	        let id = descriptor_id_from_value(&override_value)
310	            .or_else(|| id_from_path(path))
311	            .ok_or_else(|| {
312	                ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!(
313	                    "provider override {} must include id",
314	                    path.display()
315	                ))
316	            })?;
317	        ensure_id(&mut override_value, &id)?;
318	        let merged = if let Some(existing) = self.descriptors.get(&id) {
319	            let mut base = descriptor_to_value(existing)?;
320	            merge_values(&mut base, override_value);
321	            base
322	        } else {
323	            override_value
324	        };
325	        let descriptor = value_to_descriptor(merged, path)?;
326	        self.descriptors.insert(descriptor.id.clone(), descriptor);
327	        Ok(())
328	    }
329	}

354	async fn probe_descriptor(
355	    descriptor: &ProviderDescriptor,
356	    options: ProviderProbeOptions,
357	) -> ProviderProbeResult {
358	    match descriptor.kind {
359	        DescriptorKind::Cli => probe_cli_descriptor(descriptor),
360	        DescriptorKind::Http => probe_http_descriptor(descriptor, options).await,
361	        DescriptorKind::LocalHttp => probe_local_http_descriptor(descriptor, options).await,
362	        DescriptorKind::Scripted => base_probe_result(
363	            descriptor,
364	            ProbeStatus::Ok,
365	            Some("built-in".to_string()),
366	            None,
367	            "ready",
368	            None,
369	            None,
370	        ),
371	    }
372	}
373	
374	fn probe_cli_descriptor(descriptor: &ProviderDescriptor) -> ProviderProbeResult {
375	    let Some(binary) = descriptor.default_binary.as_deref() else {
376	        return base_probe_result(
377	            descriptor,
378	            ProbeStatus::Failed,
379	            None,
380	            None,
381	            "missing",
382	            Some(ProbeErrorKind::NotFound),
383	            Some("no default binary configured".to_string()),
384	        );
385	    };
386	    let Some(location) = resolve_binary(binary) else {
387	        return base_probe_result(
388	            descriptor,
389	            ProbeStatus::Failed,
390	            Some(binary.to_string()),
391	            None,
392	            "missing",
393	            Some(ProbeErrorKind::NotFound),
394	            Some(format!("{binary} not on PATH")),
395	        );
396	    };
397	    if let Some(probe) = descriptor.version_probe.as_ref()
398	        && !probe.args.is_empty()
399	    {
400	        match Command::new(&location).args(&probe.args).output() {
401	            Ok(output) => {
402	                if !output.status.success() {
403	                    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
404	                    return base_probe_result(
405	                        descriptor,
406	                        ProbeStatus::Failed,
407	                        Some(location.display().to_string()),
408	                        None,
409	                        "missing",
410	                        Some(ProbeErrorKind::ProbeFailed),
411	                        Some(trim_probe_message(&stderr)),
412	                    );
413	                }
414	                let version = trim_probe_message(&format!(
415	                    "{}{}",
416	                    String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
417	                    String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
418	                ));
419	                if let Some(expected) = probe.expect_substring.as_deref()
420	                    && !version.contains(expected)
421	                {
422	                    return base_probe_result(
423	                        descriptor,
424	                        ProbeStatus::Failed,
425	                        Some(location.display().to_string()),
426	                        Some(version),
427	                        "missing",
428	                        Some(ProbeErrorKind::VersionMismatch),
429	                        Some(format!("version output did not contain {expected}")),
430	                    );
431	                }
432	                if let Some(min) = probe.min_known_good.as_deref()
433	                    && !version_at_least(&version, min)
434	                {
435	                    return base_probe_result(
436	                        descriptor,
437	                        ProbeStatus::Failed,
438	                        Some(location.display().to_string()),
439	                        Some(version),
440	                        "missing",
441	                        Some(ProbeErrorKind::VersionMismatch),
442	                        Some(format!("version below known-good {min}")),
443	                    );
444	                }
445	                return base_probe_result(
446	                    descriptor,
447	                    ProbeStatus::Ok,
448	                    Some(location.display().to_string()),
449	                    Some(version),
450	                    "ready",
451	                    None,
452	                    None,
453	                );
454	            }
455	            Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied => {
456	                return base_probe_result(
457	                    descriptor,
458	                    ProbeStatus::Failed,
459	                    Some(location.display().to_string()),
460	                    None,
461	                    "missing",
462	                    Some(ProbeErrorKind::PermissionDenied),
463	                    Some(format!("permission denied running {binary}")),
464	                );
465	            }
466	            Err(source) => {
467	                return base_probe_result(
468	                    descriptor,
469	                    ProbeStatus::Failed,
470	                    Some(location.display().to_string()),
471	                    None,
472	                    "missing",
473	                    Some(ProbeErrorKind::ProbeFailed),
474	                    Some(source.to_string()),
475	                );
476	            }
477	        }
478	    }
479	    base_probe_result(
480	        descriptor,
481	        ProbeStatus::Ok,
482	        Some(location.display().to_string()),
483	        None,
484	        "ready",
485	        None,
486	        None,
487	    )
488	}

554	async fn ping_endpoint(descriptor: &ProviderDescriptor) -> ProviderProbeResult {
555	    let endpoint = descriptor.default_endpoint.clone().unwrap_or_default();
556	    let client = match reqwest::Client::builder()
557	        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(2))
558	        .build()
559	    {
560	        Ok(client) => client,
561	        Err(source) => {
562	            return base_probe_result(
563	                descriptor,
564	                ProbeStatus::Failed,
565	                Some(endpoint),
566	                None,
567	                "missing",
568	                Some(ProbeErrorKind::ProbeFailed),
569	                Some(source.to_string()),
570	            );
571	        }
572	    };
573	    match client.get(&endpoint).send().await {
574	        Ok(response) => base_probe_result(
575	            descriptor,
576	            ProbeStatus::Ok,
577	            Some(endpoint),
578	            Some(format!("HTTP {}", response.status())),
579	            "ready",
580	            None,
581	            None,
582	        ),
583	        Err(source) => base_probe_result(
584	            descriptor,
585	            ProbeStatus::Failed,
586	            Some(endpoint),
587	            None,
588	            "missing",
589	            Some(ProbeErrorKind::EndpointUnreachable),
590	            Some(source.to_string()),
591	        ),
592	    }
593	}

629	fn resolve_binary(binary: &str) -> Option<PathBuf> {
630	    let configured = PathBuf::from(binary);
631	    if configured.components().count() > 1 || configured.is_absolute() {
632	        return configured.exists().then_some(configured);
633	    }
634	    which::which(binary).ok()
635	}
636	
637	fn expand_home_path(path: &Path) -> PathBuf {
638	    let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(PathBuf::from) else {
639	        return path.to_path_buf();
640	    };
641	    if path == Path::new("~") {
642	        return home;
643	    }
644	    if let Ok(rest) = path.strip_prefix("~") {
645	        return home.join(rest);
646	    }
647	    path.to_path_buf()
648	}
649	
650	fn trim_probe_message(message: &str) -> String {
651	    let first_line = message
652	        .lines()
653	        .find(|line| !line.trim().is_empty())
654	        .unwrap_or("");
655	    let trimmed = first_line.trim();
656	    if trimmed.len() > 120 {
657	        format!("{}...", &trimmed[..120])
658	    } else {
659	        trimmed.to_string()
660	    }
661	}
662	
663	fn version_at_least(output: &str, minimum: &str) -> bool {
664	    let observed = first_version_tuple(output);
665	    let required = first_version_tuple(minimum);
666	    if observed.is_empty() || required.is_empty() {
667	        return output >= minimum;
668	    }
669	    compare_version_tuples(&observed, &required) != std::cmp::Ordering::Less
670	}
671	
672	fn first_version_tuple(text: &str) -> Vec<u64> {
673	    text.split(|ch: char| !ch.is_ascii_digit() && ch != '.')
674	        .find(|part| part.chars().any(|ch| ch.is_ascii_digit()))
675	        .unwrap_or("")
676	        .split('.')
677	        .filter_map(|part| part.parse::<u64>().ok())
678	        .collect()
679	}
680	
681	fn compare_version_tuples(left: &[u64], right: &[u64]) -> std::cmp::Ordering {
682	    let len = left.len().max(right.len());
683	    for index in 0..len {
684	        let l = left.get(index).copied().unwrap_or(0);
685	        let r = right.get(index).copied().unwrap_or(0);
686	        match l.cmp(&r) {
687	            std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {}
688	            ordering => return ordering,
689	        }
690	    }
691	    std::cmp::Ordering::Equal
692	}
693	
694	fn split_command_line(command: &str) -> Vec<String> {
695	    let mut args = Vec::new();
696	    let mut current = String::new();
697	    let mut quote = None::<char>;
698	    let mut escaped = false;
699	    for ch in command.chars() {
700	        if escaped {
701	            current.push(ch);
702	            escaped = false;
703	            continue;
704	        }
705	        if ch == '\\' {
706	            escaped = true;
707	            continue;
708	        }
709	        if let Some(active_quote) = quote {
710	            if ch == active_quote {
711	                quote = None;
712	            } else {
713	                current.push(ch);
714	            }
715	            continue;
716	        }
717	        match ch {
718	            '"' | '\'' => quote = Some(ch),
719	            ' ' | '\t' | '\n' => {
720	                if !current.is_empty() {
721	                    args.push(current.clone());
722	                    current.clear();
723	                }
724	            }
725	            _ => current.push(ch),
726	        }
727	    }
728	    if !current.is_empty() {
729	        args.push(current);
730	    }
731	    args
732	}

778	fn merge_values(base: &mut Value, override_value: Value) {
779	    match (base, override_value) {
780	        (Value::Table(base_table), Value::Table(override_table)) => {
781	            for (key, value) in override_table {
782	                match base_table.get_mut(&key) {
783	                    Some(base_value) => merge_values(base_value, value),
784	                    None => {
785	                        base_table.insert(key, value);
786	                    }
787	                }
788	            }
789	        }
790	        (base_value, override_value) => *base_value = override_value,
791	    }
792	}

795	fn ensure_zsh_completion_rc(completion_path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
796	    let Some(completion_dir) = completion_path.parent() else {

804	    let completion_dir = completion_dir.display();
805	    let block = format!(
806	        "\n# >>> deadreckon completion >>>\nfpath=({completion_dir} $fpath)\nautoload -Uz compinit\ncompinit\n# <<< deadreckon completion <<<\n"
807	    );
808	    if existing.contains("# >>> deadreckon completion >>>")
809	        || existing.contains(&format!("fpath=({completion_dir} $fpath)"))
810	    {
811	        println!("{} zshrc already loads completion dir", ui_ok("ready"));
812	        return Ok(());
813	    }
814	    let mut file = fs::OpenOptions::new()
815	        .create(true)
816	        .append(true)
817	        .open(&zshrc)?;
818	    file.write_all(block.as_bytes())?;
819	    println!("{} {}", ui_ok("updated"), zshrc.display());
820	    Ok(())

6923	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,

6931	        match record.mode {
6932	            CodebaseMode::Worktree => {

6934	                    "materialize is for copy/fresh runs; run was worktree",
6935	                    &format!("deadreckon apply {}", state.run_id),
6936	                )));
6937	            }
6938	            CodebaseMode::InPlace => {
6939	                return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
6940	                    "materialize is not needed; run edited the source in-place",
6941	                    "deadreckon undo",
6942	                )));
6943	            }
6944	            CodebaseMode::Copy | CodebaseMode::Fresh => {}
6945	        }
6946	    }
6947	    let library_dir = paths.library_dir(&state.scope, &state.run_id);

6949	        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::NotFound(format!(
6950	            "library missing for run {}; was promotion successful?",
6951	            state.run_id
6952	        ))));
6953	    }
6954	
6955	    let dest = absolute_dest(dest.unwrap_or_else(|| {
6956	        std::env::current_dir()
6957	            .unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from("."))
6958	            .join(run_prefix(&state.run_id))
6959	    }))?;
6960	    refuse_dest_inside_home(paths, &dest, "materialize")?;
6961	    prepare_empty_dest(&dest, force)?;
6962	
6963	    copy_tree(&library_dir, &dest)?;
6964	    if !include_manifest {
6965	        remove_if_exists(&dest.join("manifest.json"))?;
6966	    }
6967	    remove_if_exists(&dest.join(".materialized-to"))?;
6968	    write_parent_marker(
6969	        &dest.join(".deadreckon").join("parent.json"),
6970	        &materialized_parent_marker(state),
6971	    )?;
6972	    normalize_permissions(&dest)?;
6973	    append_materialized_marker(&library_dir, &dest)?;

6975	    Ok(MaterializedRun {
6976	        run_id: state.run_id.clone(),

7439	fn cleanup_candidates(
7440	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
7441	    all: bool,
7442	    include_completed: bool,
7443	    include_stale: bool,
7444	) -> Result<Vec<CleanupCandidate>> {
7445	    let scope = if all { None } else { Some(current_scope()?) };

7448	        let Ok(state) = load_run(paths, &run.run_id) else {
7449	            continue;
7450	        };
7451	        let Ok(record) = read_codebase_record(&state.working_dir) else {
7452	            continue;
7453	        };
7454	        if record.mode != CodebaseMode::Worktree {
7455	            continue;
7456	        }
7457	        let abandoned = state.run_root.join("abandoned.json").exists();
7458	        let stale = include_stale && is_stale_executing(&state);
7459	        let completed = include_completed && state.status == RunStatus::Completed && !abandoned;
7460	        if abandoned || stale || completed {
7461	            let reason = if abandoned {
7462	                "cleaned".to_string()
7463	            } else if stale {
7464	                "stale".to_string()
7465	            } else {
7466	                "completed".to_string()
7467	            };
7468	            candidates.push(CleanupCandidate {
7469	                state,
7470	                record,
7471	                reason,
7472	            });
7473	        }
7474	    }
7475	    Ok(candidates)
7476	}

6633	fn deadreckoning_course_ascii(width: usize, tick: usize) -> String {

6641	            '*'
6642	        } else if (index + tick).is_multiple_of(7) {

6648	        };

6650	    }

6741	fn set_toml_path(root: &mut toml::Value, key: &str, value: toml::Value) {
6742	    let parts = key.split('.').collect::<Vec<_>>();
6743	    let mut cursor = root;
6744	    for part in &parts[..parts.len().saturating_sub(1)] {
6745	        if !cursor.is_table() {
6746	            *cursor = toml::Value::Table(Default::default());
6747	        }
6748	        let Some(table) = cursor.as_table_mut() else {
6749	            return;
6750	        };
6751	        cursor = table
6752	            .entry((*part).to_string())
6753	            .or_insert_with(|| toml::Value::Table(Default::default()));
6754	    }
6755	    if !cursor.is_table() {
6756	        *cursor = toml::Value::Table(Default::default());
6757	    }
6758	    if let Some(table) = cursor.as_table_mut()
6759	        && let Some(last) = parts.last()
6760	    {
6761	        table.insert((*last).to_string(), value);
6762	    }
6763	}

8985	fn doc_polish_preview_text(
8986	    state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState,

9017	    Ok(out)

2909	#[derive(Debug, Default)]
2910	struct ChainAttachTuiState {
2911	    selected_step: usize,
2912	    events_scroll: u16,
2913	}
2914	
2915	impl ChainAttachTuiState {
2916	    fn clamp(&mut self, chain: &Chain) {
2917	        if chain.steps.is_empty() {
2918	            self.selected_step = 0;
2919	            self.events_scroll = 0;
2920	            return;
2921	        }
2922	        self.selected_step = self.selected_step.min(chain.steps.len() - 1);
2923	    }
2924	
2925	    fn handle_key(&mut self, key: KeyEvent, chain: &Chain) {
2926	        match key.code {
2927	            KeyCode::Up | KeyCode::Char('k') => self.scroll(-1, chain),
2928	            KeyCode::Down | KeyCode::Char('j') | KeyCode::Tab => self.scroll(1, chain),
2929	            KeyCode::PageUp => {
2930	                self.events_scroll = self.events_scroll.saturating_sub(8);
2931	            }
2932	            KeyCode::PageDown => {
2933	                self.events_scroll = self.events_scroll.saturating_add(8);
2934	            }
2935	            KeyCode::Home | KeyCode::Char('g') => {
2936	                self.selected_step = 0;
2937	                self.events_scroll = 0;
2938	            }
2939	            KeyCode::End | KeyCode::Char('G') => {
2940	                self.selected_step = chain.steps.len().saturating_sub(1);
2941	            }
2942	            _ => {}
2943	        }
2944	        self.clamp(chain);
2945	    }
2946	
2947	    fn scroll(&mut self, delta: isize, chain: &Chain) {
2948	        if chain.steps.is_empty() {
2949	            return;
2950	        }
2951	        let next = (self.selected_step as isize + delta)
2952	            .clamp(0, chain.steps.len().saturating_sub(1) as isize);
2953	        self.selected_step = next as usize;
2954	    }
2955	}

3662	        if !path.exists() {

3666	            .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json { path, source })?;

3668	            continue;

## 3. Noun Consistency

### `run` vs `task` vs `job`
- `run` is the dominant noun: e.g. "Start an unattended coding run" (447), "Cancel a running task" (872), "Resume an incomplete run" (884).
- `task` shows up in `kill` about ("Cancel a running task", cli.rs:872) and in `TOP_LEVEL_HELP` ("cancel a running task", cli.rs:34). Everywhere else: `run`.
- `job` does not appear.
- `long_about`: "runs long coding tasks in an isolated worktree" (340) mixes both nouns in one sentence.

### `turn` vs `step` vs `phase`
- `turn` is for run-internal iterations: `--from-turn` (Resume cli.rs:890), `--turn` (Undo 909, Show 922), `--max-context-turns` (Extend 811), help text "wall-clock cap for CLI-backed turns" (484).
- `step` is for chain-internal items: `--from-step` (Chain 597), `--step` (Chain 605), `--insert-at` (Chain 611), `step goals` (528), planner steps (586).
- `phase` does not appear in cli.rs.
- They are cleanly separated; no inconsistency, but doc-only readers might miss the distinction.

### `goal` vs `task` vs `prompt`
- `goal` is the dominant noun for the user's request: "Natural-language coding goal" (451), "Follow-up coding goal" (807), "Step goals or chain subcommand" (527), "Patch the selected redo step goal" (607), `--new_goal`.
- `task` only appears in "Cancel a running task" (872) and TOP_LEVEL_HELP (34). The `task` here is the *running* task, i.e. the run, not the goal. Confusing because in agent vocab "task" often equals "goal".
- `prompt` does not appear.

### `chain` vs `sequence`
- `chain` is consistent (the noun for serial coding runs).
- The verb `chain` is also a top-level command verb. `sequence` only appears as "Run a serial chain of coding goals" (523) and in `print_help_all` "run several coding steps in sequence" (627). No real noun collision but the print_help_all description uses "sequence" while clap about uses "chain".

### `provider` vs `route` vs `model`
- `provider` and `provider route` are used interchangeably:
  - "Default provider route" (360), "Provider route override" (490, 575, 819), "Provider route override for drafting" (426, 979, etc.), "Provider route for generated documentation polish" (494).
  - But also bare `--provider` help "Provider id to probe" (635), and `ConfigCommand::Provider` about: "Show or set the default provider route" (1087) while its arg help is "Provider route to make default" (1089) — internally consistent.
  - `model` is its own noun ("Model override", 428, 492, 577, 821). Never conflated.
  - `ConfigCommand::Model` about: "Show or set the model for a provider route" (1092) — uses "route".
- `route` is sometimes used solo ("Provider route override", "active route/model" in 1094) and sometimes combined ("provider route").
- `ProvidersCommand::List` about uses "providers" / "configured routes" both (1106, 1110–1113), conflating.

### `worktree` vs `branch` vs `checkout`
- `worktree` = canonical (Cleanup, Apply, Abandon).
- `branch` = git-branch attribute on a worktree run (Run `--branch` 469, Apply `--branch` 744, Finish `--branch` 694, Abandon `--keep-branch` 771, Cleanup `--keep-branch` 795).
- `checkout` shows up only in Apply about "merges the temporary `dr/...` branch back into your checkout" (241) and "source checkout" (732). It is used as a noun meaning "the user's working repo". Inconsistent: "checkout" never appears in Finish or Run help even though they target the same thing.
- "Apply target branch; defaults to the current branch" (Finish 694) vs "Target branch; defaults to the current branch" (Apply 744) — inconsistent leading word.

### `criteria` vs `acceptance` vs `done`
- Top-level `def-done` (clap name) maps to internal `Done` variant: "Write, add, show, and check done criteria in English" (416). Help calls them "done criteria" and "criteria" interchangeably (DONE_HELP 126–140).
- Top-level (hidden) `acceptance` command: "Create, refine, explain, and check project acceptance criteria" (406).
- ACCEPTANCE_HELP (142–162) calls them both "acceptance criteria" and "done" — line 143 ("Most users should use `deadreckon def-done`") and line 147 ("acceptance setup"). The compiled output goes to `.deadreckon/acceptance.yaml` (157).
- Inside `def-done` itself: help string "Compiled criteria file to show/check" (436), arg `--spec`, arg help "Acceptance spec for this run" (498) on Run command — i.e. the same file is called "acceptance spec" on `run` (498), "compiled criteria" on `def-done` (436), and just "acceptance" via `--acceptance` flag.
- `dr-gate` (159) is invoked but not named as a noun elsewhere.

- `--fresh`, `--worktree`, `--from`, `--in-place` are sibling mode switches but only `--in-place` has the safety gate (`--i-know-its-a-lot`).
- `--allow-dirty` and `--init-git` are pre-conditions; help text style differs ("Seed current dirty/untracked files into the worktree" vs "Initialize git in a plain directory before running").

## 5. Help Text Style Drift

### Capitalisation & period
Almost every `help =` string starts uppercase and has **no terminal period**. Spot-checked deviations:
- "Suppress success stdout" (591) — fine.
- All clap `about =` strings start uppercase and lack terminal periods.

Inside `after_help` (RUN_HELP/CHAIN_HELP/etc.) prose **does** use sentence periods (lines 123, 124, etc.). Internally consistent for the two contexts.

### Imperative vs descriptive
Mostly imperative ("Start...", "Cancel...", "Resume..."). Two descriptive outliers:
- `Show` about: "Show full state, provenance, and trace details for a run" (915) — imperative.
- `Status` about: "Explain the current project's latest run and next action" (927) — imperative.
- `HelpAll` about: "Show every command, including advanced commands" — imperative.

Consistent.

### Skip vs Suppress vs Don't
- `Don't` does not appear.
- `Skip`: 373, 475, 512, 535, 613, 706, 746, 791, 846 — 9 uses, 7 distinct verbs after it.
- `Suppress`: 514, 589, 591, 866 — 4 uses.
- `Do not`: 813 ("Do not include parent context") — one outlier on Extend.

Drift: `Run --no-hints` says "Suppress post-completion action prompts" while `Chain --no-hints` says "Suppress post-action hints" and `Attach --no-hints` says "Suppress post-completion action hints" — three different phrasings for the same flag.

### "override" vs "for this run"
- "Provider route override" (490, 575, 819) — bare override.
- "Model override for this run" (492) — adds scope.
- "Model override for this extended run" (821) — adds scope.
- "Model override" (577) — bare on Chain.
- "Sandbox backend override" (823) — bare.

Mild drift; the same `--model` and `--provider` flags use both styles.

### "for example"
- Used in: 361, 635, 1078, 1083, 1089 ("for example cli:codex" / "for example defaults.provider"). Consistent style.

### `INIT_HELP` etc. ordering
Each after_help block starts with `Lifecycle:` (or `Subcommands:` for Config/Acceptance/Chain) and follows with one or two sub-sections. Ordering not 100% uniform:
- INIT_HELP, DOCTOR_HELP, RUN_HELP, ATTACH_HELP, KILL_HELP, RESUME_HELP, UNDO_HELP, SHOW_HELP, STATUS_HELP, IMPORT_HELP, FINISH_HELP, MATERIALIZE_HELP, APPLY_HELP, ABANDON_HELP, CLEANUP_HELP, EXTEND_HELP all open with `Lifecycle:`.
- CONFIG_HELP opens with `Subcommands:` then `Lifecycle:` (69–79). LIBRARY_HELP same (205–213).
- ACCEPTANCE_HELP opens with a free-form paragraph (143) before `Subcommands:` (145).
- CHAIN_HELP opens with `Chain subcommands:` (variant of `Subcommands:`, 165) — different header.
- COMPLETION_HELP opens with `Lifecycle:` (46).
- DONE_HELP has `Common actions:` then `What it means:` (131, 138).
- PROVIDERS_HELP starts with `Lifecycle:` (93).

### Run-id description drift
The standard phrase is "Run id, unique prefix, or latest":
- Finish 681, Materialize 720, Apply 737, Abandon 770, Doc 839, Attach 865, Kill 877, Resume 889, Show 920 — all match.
- Cleanup: "Optional run id, unique prefix, or latest" (783–784) — adds "Optional".
- Status: "Optional run id, unique prefix, or latest" (932) — adds "Optional".
- Extend: "Parent run id, unique prefix, or latest" (806) — adds "Parent".
- Undo `--run`: "Run id, unique prefix, or latest; defaults to current project's latest" (cli.rs:905–906) — appends a semicolon clause.

Reasonable variation, but Undo's `--run` is the only place where the run-id is a long flag rather than a positional arg.

## 7. Hidden Commands Visible Through Other Channels

Hidden via `hide = true`:
- `Acceptance` (cli.rs:405) — visible in print_help_all "inspect and advanced".
- `Library` (664) — visible in print_help_all.
- `Materialize` (713) — surfaced under alias `export` in print_help_all (line 651 in main.rs).
- `Apply` (730) — visible in print_help_all.
- `Abandon` (763) — visible in print_help_all.
- `Doc` (832) — visible in print_help_all.
- `Show` (913) — visible in print_help_all.
- `Undo` (897) — visible in print_help_all.
- `Import` (941) — visible in print_help_all.

These hidden commands also retain `visible_alias`/`visible_aliases`:
| Hidden cmd | visible_alias(es) |
|---|---|
| Acceptance | none |
| Library | artifacts |
| Materialize | export, copy-out |
| Apply | keep |
| Abandon | discard |
| Doc | docs |
| Show | inspect |
| Undo | restore |
| Import | none |

A `visible_alias` on a hidden command still hides both the canonical and the alias from `--help` (clap behaviour: hide propagates to the whole command, but the alias is still callable). This means `deadreckon --help` shows none of: acceptance, library, materialize, apply, abandon, doc, show, undo, import — *nor* their aliases (`artifacts`, `export`, `copy-out`, `keep`, `discard`, `docs`, `inspect`, `restore`). They only surface via the hand-written `print_help_all`.

## Inconsistencies (summary)

- **Chain, config, list, detect, providers missing from `print_top_help` / `TOP_LEVEL_HELP`** (main.rs:544–616, cli.rs:15–43) although they are non-hidden top-level commands. A user typing `deadreckon --help` sees no mention of `chain`, the second-most-prominent execution verb in CHAIN_HELP (cli.rs:164–185).
- **Detect and providers missing from `print_help_all`** (main.rs:618–670) — every non-hidden command should appear; these are setup commands that exist in clap (cli.rs:629–650) but are invisible to users browsing help.
- **`config` placed in "inspect and advanced"** by print_help_all (main.rs:655) but `next_help_heading = "Setup"` in clap (cli.rs:377). Inconsistent grouping.
- **`chain` description drift**: clap says "Run a serial chain of coding goals" (cli.rs:523); print_help_all says "run several coding steps in sequence" (main.rs:627). Three nouns change.
- **`attach` description drift**: clap "Attach the live terminal UI to a run" (860) vs print_help_all "watch a run in the TUI" (628). The text uses the *alias* (`watch`) rather than the canonical verb. Same drift exists in TOP_LEVEL_HELP "watch a run in the TUI" (27).
- **`kill` says "Cancel a running task"** (cli.rs:872) — only place in cli.rs where a run is called a "task". TOP_LEVEL_HELP and print_top_help echo it (34, 585).
- **`finish` says "completed work"** in TOP_LEVEL_HELP / print_top_help (29, 575) and print_help_all (631), while clap says "completed run" (676). "Work" appears nowhere else.
- **`cleanup` description drift**: clap "Clean stale or temporary deadreckon worktrees" (cli.rs:779); print_top_help/print_help_all "remove stale or completed worktrees" (35, 585, 641). "Temporary" vs "completed" name different states. CLEANUP_HELP (250–256) calls them "abandoned, stale, or completed temporary worktrees" — three states.
- **`acceptance` description drift**: clap "Create, refine, explain, and check project acceptance criteria" (cli.rs:406); print_help_all "advanced compatibility command for done criteria" (660). Wildly different framings of the same command.
- **`abandon` vs `discard` verb crossover**: ABANDON_HELP (243–248) uses "Discard removes a run's temporary worktree…" — i.e. the help for canonical `abandon` describes the action as "discard". print_help_all calls it "discard a temporary worktree run" (644). The canonical name is barely used in the help body.
- **`apply` mentions `dr/...` branches in body** (cli.rs:241) but the term `dr/` appears nowhere else; the prefix is undocumented in the Run command help where the branch is created.
- **`apply` has no `--force`**, while `Finish` has `--force` (overwrite export dest), `Abandon` has `--force` (override executing), `Cleanup` has `--force` (kill processes), `Kill` has `--force` (escalate signal). Five meanings.
- **`--strategy` (Apply, Finish) vs `--apply-strategy` (Chain)** — same concept, different flag name (cli.rs:553, 692, 741).
- **`--max-spend` vs `--budget-cap`** (cli.rs:481, 854) — same concept (spend cap in USD), different name. `Doc` is the only command that uses `--budget-cap`.
- **`--from` (Run) vs `--from-file`/`--from-stdin` (Chain)** — the flag prefix `--from` means "copy this dir" on Run (459) and "read goals from <X>" on Chain (529–532). Cross-command name collision.
- **`--branch`** means create-new on Run (469), destination on Apply (744), destination on Finish (694).
- **`--all` has at least three semantics**: across-projects (List 660, Library 1156, Status 935), across-scopes (Cleanup 785, Chain 617), across-providers (ProvidersCommand 1112).
- **`--no-confirm` and `--yes` both exist on Run and Chain** with semantically distinct but overlapping meaning ("skip preview" vs "skip safety prompts"). Likely to confuse — neither help string clearly disambiguates.
- **`--no-hints` help text** differs across three commands that use the same flag name: "Suppress post-completion action prompts" (Run 514), "Suppress post-action hints" (Chain 589), "Suppress post-completion action hints" (Attach 866). Pick one phrasing.
- **`--include-manifest` help text** differs ("Keep manifest.json in exported output" Finish 686 vs "Keep manifest.json in the exported output" Materialize 725) — trivial article drift.
- **`Extend` lacks `--doc-provider`** despite owning `--no-docs` and `--doc-skill` (825–828). `Run` and `Doc` both have `--doc-provider` (494, 853).
- **`Undo` uses `--run <id>` as a long flag** (cli.rs:903–907) instead of a positional, breaking the pattern set by every other completed-run command (Finish, Materialize, Apply, Abandon, Cleanup, Extend, Doc, Attach, Kill, Resume, Show all use positional `run_id`).
- **`Detect` uses positional `id`** (cli.rs:634–636) but everything else of similar shape uses `run_id` or a flag.
- **Status' `--all`** (cli.rs:933–937) inverts the convention — every other `--all` widens the *filter*; on `status` it changes the *target* (the global latest run rather than the project-scoped latest).
- **`next_help_heading` buckets vs hand-written headings**: clap uses Title Case ("Setup", "Run Lifecycle", "Completed Run Actions", "Cleanup And Recovery", "Inspect And Import", "Acceptance", "Done Criteria"); print_top_help uses Sentence case ("Core lifecycle:", "Continue or recover:", "More help:"); print_help_all uses lowercase ("core lifecycle", "continue and recover", "inspect and advanced"). Three styles for the same concept.
- **`acceptance` vs `def-done` collision**: both exist (def-done is the canonical user-facing entry per ACCEPTANCE_HELP line 143), and `def-done` writes "done criteria" while `acceptance` writes "acceptance criteria" — but both emit to `.deadreckon/acceptance.yaml` (157). Two command names, two nouns, one underlying artefact.
- **`acceptance check` (cli.rs:1048) vs `def-done check` (subverb under Done's positional, see DONE_HELP 119) vs top-level `doctor` alias `check` (cli.rs:622–627)**: the verb `check` is overloaded three ways.
- **`AcceptanceCommand::Setup`** (cli.rs:976) name collides with top-level `Init`'s `setup` alias (cli.rs:353). `deadreckon setup ...` runs init; `deadreckon acceptance setup ...` runs acceptance setup.
- **`AcceptanceCommand::Init`** (1004) name collides with top-level `Init` (351). `acceptance init` and `init` mean different things.
- **`--preset`** values include `auto, basic, build, test, rust, node, static-site, browser, playwright, vite, nextjs, python` per ACCEPTANCE_HELP (162), but `AcceptancePreset` enum (1064–1071) only declares `Auto, Rust, Node, StaticSite, Basic`. Six packs listed in help text are not valid `--preset` values.
- **`Chain`'s positional `args: Vec<String>`** (527) holds both *step goals* and *chain subcommand names* (`plan`, `run`, `attach`, etc., per CHAIN_HELP). This makes Chain a verb-overloaded command, not a clap-subcommand-driven one, while `Acceptance`, `Config`, `Providers`, `Library`, `Completion` all use proper `#[command(subcommand)]`. Inconsistent design.
- **`Done`'s positional `args: Vec<String>`** (cli.rs:420–425) similarly mixes "plain-English criteria" and sub-verbs (`add`, `check`, `show`), again unlike the canonical subcommand approach. DONE_HELP (131–136) lists those verbs but they are not first-class clap subcommands.
- **`completion` has both subcommand-style invocation (`completion bash`) and an alias `completions`** (cli.rs:393–402). The subcommand `Install` is the default when none provided (main.rs:673), which is a non-obvious convention — Completion is the only command whose subcommand is optional with a fallback.
- **`Chain`'s `--extend` flag** (cli.rs:607–608) shares its name with the top-level `Extend` command (798). On `chain redo`, `--extend "new goal"` patches a step; on top level, `extend latest "new goal"` creates a follow-up. Same word, two scopes.
- **`--reapply`** (Chain, 609) and `apply`/`reapply` family have no documented relationship in cli.rs.
- **`def-done` arg `args` help "Plain-English criteria, or add/check/show"** (cli.rs:423) — undocumented that the same positional can hold a subverb. This is the only place the verb-overloading is hinted at.
- **`hide = true` on Show, Apply, Abandon, Materialize, Library, Doc, Undo, Import, Acceptance** removes them and their aliases from `--help`. Users discover them only by reading `help-all`, README, HOWTO, or trial-and-error. This contradicts the README/HOWTO which document them as first-class (`HOWTO.md:362` `deadreckon apply <run-id>`, etc.).
- **Help-all alias-as-canonical**: `print_help_all` (main.rs:651) lists `export` (alias) rather than `materialize` (canonical). This is the only command surfaced under its alias name in help-all. Other hidden commands appear under their canonical names (apply, abandon, show, library, doc, undo, import, acceptance).
- **`finish`'s after-help block (FINISH_HELP, cli.rs:214–225) lists run-mode→action routing as `worktree run -> apply`, `fresh/copy run -> export`, `in-place run -> show review guidance`**. The verb `export` here refers to the materialize-aliased command; "show review guidance" is not a command name and has no corresponding clap verb.
- **`detect` vs `doctor` vs `providers list --all`** — three different commands for "what's installed/configured?", with overlapping concerns:
  - `doctor` (622): all providers, CLI binaries, sandboxes, disk, OS.
  - `detect` (629): providers only, credential/PATH probe, optional `--ping`.
  - `providers list` (1106): registry metadata only.
  No help text cross-links them.
- **`Resume`** has `--max-wall-seconds` but no `--max-spend` (cli.rs:887–894), while `Extend` has both (815–818). Recovering a run cannot raise its budget; creating a new follow-up can. Possibly intentional, not documented.
- **`Chain --branch-policy stack|base|merge`** vs top-level Apply/Finish `--strategy squash|merge|cherry-pick`: the word `merge` is in both enums with different referents (a branch-arrangement strategy in chain; a git merge strategy in apply).

# Deadreckon TUI Audit Report

Two ratatui TUI surfaces exist:
- **Run/Attach TUI** — `attach_tui` at `crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:10123`, render entry `render_attach` at line 12154. Used by `deadreckon run` (when not detached) and `deadreckon attach <run-id>`.
- **Chain Attach TUI** — `chain_attach_tui` at `crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:2807`, render entry `render_chain_attach` at line 2957. Used by `deadreckon chain attach <id>`.

`tui_events.rs` is a JSONL/broadcast event feed for the Run/Attach TUI; it has no rendering surface itself.

No `Tabs` widget is used in either TUI.

#### Processes panel lines — `process_lines` at `main.rs:12917-12929`:
- per-pid format: `` `{pid} {status} {command}` `` where status is `alive` or `dead`
- empty: `` `no supervised pids` ``
- `live_pid` (`main.rs:10851-10876`) populates command as `"alive"` literal (fallback) or `"not running"` when not alive

Inconsistency between the two: a process row says `"alive"` / `"dead"`, but its command column can independently say `"alive"` (when ps stdout is empty) or `"not running"` (when not alive). So a dead pid prints `"{pid} dead not running"` and an alive pid may print `"{pid} alive alive"`.

**Line 2: `footer_for_state`** at `main.rs:12278-12313` — see key bindings below.

#### Turn timer label — `turn_timer` at `main.rs:13011-13070`, formats:

## Inconsistencies

### Status label capitalization / tense

- `main.rs:12344` shows `RunStatus::Completed → "complete"` (adjective) in the Run TUI footer, while every other surface uses `"completed"` (past tense): chain status (`3942`), chain step status (`3953`), chain event label (`3127`), CompletionAction notice success status `"finished"` (`10449`). User-visible impact: the run footer says "deadreckoning complete" while elsewhere the same state reads "completed".
- The post-action notice uses `"finished"` for success and `"failed"` for error (`main.rs:10449`), but the run footer status line uses `"failed"` for `RunStatus::Failed` (`12345`) — so "failed" is overloaded: it means both "the run errored" and "the action errored".

### Glyph collisions

- `chain_step_dot` returns `●` for both `Running` and `Applied` (`main.rs:3964, 3968`). User-visible impact: a step that is currently running is indistinguishable from a step that has been applied in the steps panel; user must read the status label column to tell them apart.

### Color collisions

- Yellow is used for three unrelated semantics: spend/context threshold mid-range (`13084`), acceptance `DefaultGate` AND `Configured` (`12475`), and Markdown inline code spans (`12759`). Within the same panel-set, "context is yellow" and "acceptance is yellow" mean entirely different things.
- `acceptance_color` collapses `DefaultGate` and `Configured` to the same Yellow (`main.rs:12475`) even though one indicates an inferred default and the other a user-configured spec.
- Blue: used for run-status second half (`12331`) AND for markdown links (`12730-12731, 12736`). When the docs panel is open, links and the footer "rest" share the same color but only links are underlined.
- Cyan: used for focused-panel border (`12942`), markdown H1 (`12817`), markdown list bullets (`12691`), header bullet `▸` (`12830`), running acceptance block (`12476`), AND the bold first half of the run footer status line (`12328`). At least five unrelated meanings.

### Footer / help text inconsistencies

- Run TUI in-progress footer (`12310`) advertises `Detach: q Esc Ctrl-D  |  Focus: Tab  |  Scroll: j/k Up/Down PgUp/PgDn mouse` (capitalized prefixes, no brackets around keys).
- Run TUI completion footer (`12296-12306`) uses bracketed `[d] Docs  [a] Apply ...` with capitalized verbs and `Tab focus  j/k scroll  q detach` (lowercase, no brackets) — two different conventions in the same TUI.
- Chain TUI footer (`3111`) uses bracketed lowercase verbs `[Enter] drill  [r] redo  [e] extend ...` and unbracketed `j/k move` — inconsistent with Run TUI's `j/k scroll`.
- Chain TUI paused footer (`3107`) uses `|` separators and "try:" hints, Run TUI footers use `|` separators too but no "try:" form.
- Chain snapshot footer (`2804`) advertises `[q] quit` but Chain TUI footer says `[Ctrl-D/q/Esc] detach` — same key, two different verbs (quit vs detach).
- Chain TUI footer advertises `[Enter] drill`, but the snapshot footer omits Enter entirely.

### Header field formatting inconsistencies

- Chain TUI header uses `spend ${total:.6}/${cap:.6}` (six decimals, `main.rs:3015`); snapshot uses `spend: ${total:.2}/${cap:.2}` (two decimals, `2772-2785`). Same chain renders different precision depending on TTY.
- Chain TUI header uses `status {label}` (space separator, `3015`); snapshot uses `status: {label}` (colon-space, `2772`).
- Chain TUI policy line `policy branch={p} apply={m} strategy={s} on-fail={f}` (`3015-3028`) vs snapshot `policy: {p} | apply={m} | on-fail={f}` (`2787-2793`) — different separators, snapshot omits `strategy`.

### Separator inconsistencies (TUI text)

- Run TUI activity-feed turn summary uses double-space separators: `turn {N}  {model}  {tokens} tokens  ${cost}` (`12504-12506`).
- Run TUI event lines use single spaces: `turn {N} {tool_name} {tool_call_id} started` (`12969`).
- Run TUI trace lines use double-space: `trace turn {N}  {event}  {ms}ms` (`12566-12568`).
- Run TUI footers use `  |  ` (space-pipe-space-space, `12290, 12296`) but Chain TUI paused footer uses `  | ` (space-pipe-space, no trailing extra space, `3107`).
- Run TUI deadreckoning-status line uses double-space between fields: `deadreckoning {status}  turn {label}  {phase}  {course}` (`12352`).
- Chain activity line uses single spaces: `{ts} {event_label}{step}{detail}` (`3093-3098`).

### Unit / format inconsistencies

- Wall time displayed as `{:.0}s` in turn summary (`12510`) but `{}s` (no precision specifier on the raw float) in `event_line` SpendDelta (`12990`) and a separate non-metered branch (`12993`) — meaning event lines may show `wall 1.234567s` while turn-summary rows of the same record show `wall 1s`.
- `format_age` uses `s` / `m` / `h` single-letter suffixes (`13098-13104`); turn timer uses `Ns running` / `Ns done` (`13030, 13040, 13047, 13050, 13067`) but also returns bare `"done"` (`13069`) and bare `"-"` (`13023`) — no suffix-vs-fallback consistency.
- `trace turn ... {:?}ms` uses Rust Debug formatting on `Option<u64>` (`12567`) — the user sees raw `Some(123)` or `None` strings in the activity feed.
- `format_bytes` uses single-letter `B` / `K` / `M` (no `i`, no `iB`) (`13107-13115`); `format_count` uses `K` / `M` as decimal SI for tokens (`13117-13125`) — same letters, two different unit conventions in one TUI.
- Spend amounts: gauge label uses `${:.6}` (`12380`), `event_line` uses `${:.6}` (`12989`), snapshot uses `${:.2}` (`2772-2785`).

### Process-row redundancy

- Process row at `main.rs:12925` formats `"{pid} {status} {command}"` where `status` is `"alive"`/`"dead"`. The `command` field separately falls back to literal `"alive"` (`10867`) or `"not running"` (`10869`). So a dead pid appears as `"42 dead not running"` (status + command saying the same thing twice) and a no-ps alive pid as `"42 alive alive"`.

### "Detach" vs "quit" wording

- `attach_should_quit` (`10301-10304`) returns true for q/Esc/Ctrl-D. Run TUI in-progress footer calls this "Detach" (`12310`); completion footer calls it "q detach" (`12296`); chain TUI calls it "detach" (`3111`); chain snapshot calls it "quit" (`2804`). Same action, four different phrasings across surfaces.

### Selection marker style (Chain TUI)

- Selected step has `>` styled in `Color::Cyan` (`3052`). Other rows have a space styled in Cyan (visually invisible but still spends a styled span). No background highlight, no bold — relies entirely on a single Cyan `>` glyph.

### Focus indication asymmetry

- Run/Attach TUI marks the focused panel with both `*` prefix in the title (`panel_title` at `12948-12957`) AND Cyan border (`panel_border_style` at `12940-12946`).
- Chain Attach TUI has no focused-panel concept — neither the steps panel nor the chain-activity panel reacts to the user's selection state, even though the steps panel has a selected row.

### Spend gauge color exception is uncommented

- `meter_color` (`13072-13078`) switches to `Color::Magenta` only when `state.pause_reason == Some("spend cap reached")` — a magic string. Any other pause reason keeps the threshold color. No legend / footer mentions what Magenta means.

### Acceptance status label tense mismatch with everything else

- Acceptance block: `default gate`, `configured`, `running`, `passed`, `failed` (`12437-12462`).
- Run footer status uses adjective `complete` rather than past tense `completed`.
- Chain step labels use past tense `completed`, `applied`, `skipped`, `undone`. The TUI mixes adjective/gerund/past-tense across panels.

### Markdown rendering vs. plain text panels

- Markdown rendering inside the docs view colors inline code Yellow+Bold (`12758-12761`) — but the same Yellow is used for the "context" threshold band; a doc that mentions `` `90% utilization` `` will look identical to a critical context warning.

### Polling cadence

- Run/Attach TUI polls every 200ms (`10158`); Chain Attach TUI polls every 250ms (`2821`). User-visible: the chain timeline animates 20% slower than the run activity.

### "turn {N}" formatting

- Run TUI activity feed has `turn {N}` for events and `turn {turn_label}` (a free-form string like `"42s running"`) in the footer status (`12352`). The literal token `turn ` therefore appears with two different right-hand types in the same screen (integer vs duration phrase).

# User-Facing Surface Matrix

**Status:** Draft for polish-pass goal.
**Scope:** Every action a user can take and every state a user can land in across `deadreckon`, with the exact text/colors/glyphs they see, sourced from code.
**Method:** Audit of `crates/deadreckon/src/cli.rs`, `crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs` (~14.3 K lines), `crates/deadreckon/src/tui_events.rs`, `crates/deadreckon-core/src/{state,chain,gate,events}.rs`, plus help-text constants. Five parallel audit agents fed by direct reads.
**Read this as:** evidence for a follow-up goal that polishes each inconsistency. Each row is a hand-hold for the next agent: a current observable behaviour + a file:line so the fix is unambiguous.

> Conventions used below:
> - `text` in backticks is a verbatim string from code.
> - "stdout / stderr" notes which stream a string lands on at runtime.
> - File:line citations target the source file at the time of audit (commit `455b91a`).
> - ANSI codes use raw SGR notation (e.g. `1;36` = bold cyan).
> - **Bold rows** in inconsistency tables indicate the user can observe both variants in a single session.

## 1. State vocabulary

These are the words the user sees in `status`, `list`, `show`, TUI, and JSON output. Inconsistencies here cascade everywhere else.

### 1.1 `RunStatus` — single-run lifecycle

| Variant | Serialized | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Pending` | `pending` | `crates/deadreckon-core/src/state.rs:21-42` | kebab-case |
| `Planned` | `planned` | same | |
| `Executing` | `executing` | same | **See §1.5 collision with `ChainStatus::Running`** |
| `Completed` | `completed` | same | |
| `Failed` | `failed` | same | |
| `Killed` | `killed` | same | |

### 1.2 `ChainStatus` — chain lifecycle

| Variant | Serialized | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Pending` | `pending` | `crates/deadreckon-core/src/chain.rs:18-28` | snake_case |
| `Running` | `running` | same | not `executing` |
| `Paused` | `paused` | same | runs have no paused state |
| `Completed` | `completed` | same | |
| `Failed` | `failed` | same | |
| `Killed` | `killed` | same | |
| `Undone` | `undone` | same | runs have no undone state |

### 1.3 `ChainStepStatus` — chain step lifecycle

| Variant | Serialized | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Pending` | `pending` | `crates/deadreckon-core/src/chain.rs:30-40` | |
| `Running` | `running` | same | |
| `Completed` | `completed` | same | |
| `Failed` | `failed` | same | |
| `Skipped` | `skipped` | same | only valid for steps, not chains/runs |
| `Applied` | `applied` | same | terminal happy-path for a step |
| `Undone` | `undone` | same | |

### 1.4 `PhaseStatus` — phase ticker inside a run

| Variant | Serialized | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Pending`/`Planned`/`Executing`/`Completed`/`Failed` | lowercase | `crates/deadreckon-core/src/state.rs:47-68` |

Phases use `Executing`, matching runs but not chains.

### 1.5 Cross-cutting state inconsistencies

| Concept | Run/phase word | Chain word | Where user sees both | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "actively progressing" | `executing` | `running` | `status` of a run vs `chain status` in the same project | `state.rs:35` vs `chain.rs:22` |
| "happy-path end" | `completed` | `completed` (chain) / `applied` (step) | `chain show` mixes both | `chain.rs:24,37` |
| "cancelled by user" | `killed` | `killed` | aligned | |
| **collision** | a phase says `executing`, while the parent chain TUI sub-row says `running` | both in the same chain attach view | `main.rs:3115-3133` event labels + `state.rs:35` |

### 1.6 Chain event labels

`chain_event_label()` at `crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:3115-3134` maps:

| Enum | Label string |
|---|---|
| `ChainCreated` | `created` |
| `ChainStepStarted` | `step started` |
| `ChainRunCompleted` | `run completed` |
| `ChainApplyStarted` | `apply started` |
| `ChainApplied` | `applied` |
| `ChainApplyRefused` | `apply refused` |
| `ChainStepFailed` | `step failed` |
| `ChainPaused` | `paused` |
| `ChainResumed` | `resumed` |
| `ChainKilled` | `killed` |
| `ChainCompleted` | `completed` |
| `ChainUndoStarted` | `undo started` |
| `ChainUndoneStep` | `undone step` |
| `ChainHookInvoked` | `hook` |
| `ChainStepExtended` | `extended` |
| `ChainStepRedone` | `redone` |

Inconsistency: noun-verb pairing is asymmetric.
- "step started" / "step failed" / "run completed" all use noun-first.
- "undone step" reverses to adjective-noun while sibling `undo started` reads as a phrase.
- `hook` is a bare noun (no verb), every other label has either a verb or verb-phrase.
- `apply started` vs `undo started` are parallel; `apply refused` has no equivalent for undo refusal.

| `import` | — | Inspect And Import | **yes** | `Import read-only history from another coding tool` |

### 2.1 Observations on visibility

`hide = true` removes the command from the top-level help, but **its aliases are still functional and discoverable** (e.g. `keep`, `discard`, `export`). Users who learn an alias from after-help text (`APPLY_HELP` says `deadreckon discard latest`) see the alias word but `--help` will not list the canonical. This produces "ghost commands": working verbs invisible to discovery.

Specifically hidden but reachable via alias used in another command's after-help:
- `apply` (via `APPLY_HELP` in `cli.rs:235-241`, after-help on the hidden `Apply` command itself).
- `abandon` (via `ABANDON_HELP` `cli.rs:243-248`, after-help of hidden command; the visible-from-elsewhere alias is `discard`).
- `materialize` (after-help recommends `deadreckon export latest --dest ...`).
- `doc` (after-help recommends `deadreckon doc latest`).
- `show` (after-help across many other helpers references `deadreckon show latest`).

Net: the user can't find these via `--help`, but the canonical examples in *other* commands' after-helps mention them. Inconsistent "command exists / command discoverable" boundary.

### 2.2 Acceptance vs def-done duplication

Both `acceptance` (hidden) and `def-done` (visible) operate on the same `.deadreckon/acceptance.yaml`. The hidden `acceptance` exposes `setup`, `add`, `init --preset`, `draft`, `refine`, `explain`, `check`; the visible `def-done` accepts free text or `add`/`check`/`show`. Users are told to prefer `def-done` (`ACCEPTANCE_HELP` line 1, `cli.rs:143`). Yet `def-done show` exists on def-done but is not documented as a counterpart to `acceptance explain`. The two surfaces are not name-aligned.
