## 3. Verb pairs and synonyms

### 3.1 Pairs explicitly defined as `visible_alias` (the user is told both work)

| Concept | Canonical | Alias | First-use evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Configure | `init` | `setup` | `cli.rs:353` |
| Read or write config | `config` | `settings` | `cli.rs:378` |
| List runs | `list` | `runs` | `cli.rs:653` |
| Watch live | `attach` | `watch` | `cli.rs:860` |
| Cancel | `kill` | `stop` | `cli.rs:871` |
| Pick back up | `resume` | `continue` | `cli.rs:883` |
| Restore | `undo` | `restore` | `cli.rs:898` |
| Inspect | `show` | `inspect` | `cli.rs:914` |
| Explain next | `status` | `next` | `cli.rs:926` |
| Keep worktree | `apply` | `keep` | `cli.rs:731` |
| Throw away worktree | `abandon` | `discard` | `cli.rs:764` |
| Sweep | `cleanup` | `prune`, `clean` | `cli.rs:778` |
| Export copy | `materialize` | `export`, `copy-out` | `cli.rs:714` |
| Continue work | `extend` | `follow-up` | `cli.rs:800` |
| Promoted artifacts | `library` | `artifacts` | `cli.rs:666` |
| All commands | `help-all` | `commands` | `cli.rs:388` |
| Completions | `completion` | `completions` | `cli.rs:395` |
| Doctor | `doctor` | `check` | `cli.rs:624` |
| Print run docs | `doc` | `docs` | `cli.rs:833` |

### 3.2 De facto synonyms used in after-help only (alias yet "preferred name")

Lines in `cli.rs:235-256` repeatedly use `keep` / `discard` / `export` rather than canonicals (`apply` / `abandon` / `materialize`). Users learning from after-help adopt the alias.

| File:line | Says | Should map to canonical |
|---|---|---|
| `cli.rs:239` | `deadreckon discard latest` | `abandon` |
| `cli.rs:245` | `deadreckon discard latest` | `abandon` |
| `cli.rs:229` | `deadreckon export latest --dest …` | `materialize` |
| `cli.rs:107` | `deadreckon attach latest` | `attach` (canonical) |
| `cli.rs:320` | `deadreckon next` | `status` |
| `cli.rs:106` | `deadreckon next` | `status` |

The mix of alias and canonical inside the same help block (`RUN_HELP` cli.rs:102-124 uses `attach`/`next`/`finish` mixing canonical/alias forms) means users will copy whichever word they hit first.

### 3.3 Hidden synonyms (in code but not user-visible)

`HelpAll` has alias `commands`. `Completion` has `completions`. Both are visible aliases so they're listed in 3.1, but note: the top-level help text (`TOP_LEVEL_HELP` lines 39-40) lists `help-all` AND `commands` as separate entries. This implies they're different, when they're aliases:

\```
help-all    show every command, including advanced commands
commands    alias for help-all
\```

Showing an alias as if it were a separate command is unique to `help-all`; no other alias is given its own line in top-level help.

### 3.4 Verb pairs **not** aliased that the user expects to be

These are verbs where two distinct commands sound interchangeable:
- `status` vs `show` — both inspect a run, different depth. Could read as synonyms.
- `def-done` vs `acceptance` — same backing store, parallel surfaces (§2.2).
- `materialize` vs `apply` — both finish a run; routed by `finish` based on mode. The TUI/CLI does not signal which one applies until the user picks `finish`.
- `cleanup` vs `abandon` — `abandon <id>` cleans one run; `cleanup` sweeps many. Surface-similar enough to be confusing.

## 4. Noun consistency

(Populated from cross-file scan; deeper detail to follow in §13.)

| Concept | Words observed | First evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Unit of work | `run`, `task` (in `KILL_HELP`/`Kill.about`), `job` (none) | `cli.rs:872` calls it "running task"; everywhere else "run" |
| Sub-unit | `turn` (resume `--from-turn`), `step` (chain `--from-step`), `phase` (`PhaseStatus`) | `cli.rs:597`, `cli.rs:891`, `state.rs:49` |
| User intent | `goal` (run/extend), `request` (acceptance setup), `criterion` (acceptance add) | `cli.rs:452`, `cli.rs:977`, `cli.rs:992` |
| Multi-step plan | `chain` everywhere | OK |
| Provider id | `route` (in flags `--provider <route>`), `descriptor` (in `providers list`), `provider`, `model` | `cli.rs:361`, `LIST_HELP`, etc. |
| Working tree | `worktree`, `branch`, `checkout` | `APPLY_HELP` cli.rs:241 |
| Definition of done | `acceptance`, `done`, `def-done`, `criteria`, `criterion` | `cli.rs:142-162` |
| Promoted output | `library`, `artifact`, `promotion` | `LIBRARY_HELP` cli.rs:205-212 |
| Run mode | `worktree`, `fresh`, `copy`, `in-place` | `RUN_HELP` cli.rs:122-124 |

### 4.1 "Task" leaks

`KILL_HELP` at `cli.rs:287-293` says "Cancel a running task". This is the only place `task` appears in user copy. Elsewhere we say "run". Inconsistency: a user types `kill` thinking they cancel a "task", then in `status` sees "run".

### 4.2 "Turn" vs "Step"

A single run uses turns (`Resume --from-turn`, `Undo --turn`, `Show --turn`). A chain uses steps (`Chain --from-step`, chain step status). These are different layers — but `chain extend --step` and `--insert-at` mix with a step-level `--turn` would be confusing. Worse, "turn" is also used in `--max-context-turns` on Extend, where it refers to **parent run turns**, not chain steps. (`cli.rs:811-812`)

### 4.3 "Route" / "provider" / "model"

`--provider <ROUTE>` (cli.rs:360 `Default provider route, for example cli:codex or cli:claude-code`) — the flag is named `--provider` but the help calls it a `route`. `config provider` is a subcommand. `providers list` is a different command. The user sees three different surfaces all named differently for the same concept.

## 5. Flag and option consistency

### 5.1 Default-value drift

| Command | Flag | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `init` | `--max-spend` | `10.0` (cli.rs:367) |
| `init` | `--sandbox` | `auto` (cli.rs:369) |
| `run` | `--skill` | `default-coding` (cli.rs:504) |
| `chain` | `--branch-policy` | `stack` (cli.rs:543) |
| `chain` | `--apply-mode` | `auto` (cli.rs:547) |
| `chain` | `--apply-strategy` | `squash` (cli.rs:553) |
| `chain` | `--on-fail` | `stop` (cli.rs:561) |
| `chain` | `--circuit-breaker-threshold` | `2` (cli.rs:567) |
| `chain` | `--sandbox` | `auto` (cli.rs:579) |
| `chain` | `--n` | `4` (cli.rs:585) |
| `apply` | `--strategy` | `squash` (cli.rs:743) |
| `finish` | `--strategy` | `squash` (cli.rs:693) |
| `doc` | `--kind` | `Narrative` (cli.rs:840) |

The strategy default is consistent at `squash`. The chain sandbox lacks `Option<>` (it always sends `auto`) while `run`/`extend` use `Option<String>` (default deferred to config). User-visible effect: passing `--sandbox` explicitly on chain is required to override; on `run` it falls through to config.

### 5.2 Confirmation flag mix

- `--yes` exists on `run` (cli.rs:476) and `chain` (cli.rs:536) — skips preview confirmation.
- `--no-confirm` exists on `run` (cli.rs:513), `chain` (cli.rs:614), `init` (cli.rs:372), `finish` (cli.rs:707), `apply` (cli.rs:747), `cleanup` (cli.rs:791), `doc` (cli.rs:847).
- `--yes` and `--no-confirm` coexist on `run` and `chain` — what's the difference? `--yes` skips the run preview; `--no-confirm` skips the safety prompts. Two flags for arguably the same thing on the same command. (Verified `cli.rs:475-476` and `cli.rs:512-513`.)

### 5.3 `--force` semantics

| Command | What `--force` does |
|---|---|
| `init`/`config` | n/a |
| `run` (n/a) | — |
| `kill` | "Escalate subprocess termination" (cli.rs:879) |
| `chain` (in kill context) | "Force kill without SIGTERM grace" (cli.rs:603) |
| `materialize` | "Overwrite a non-empty destination" (cli.rs:723) |
| `finish` | "Overwrite a non-empty export destination" (cli.rs:684) |
| `abandon` | "Clean even if the run is still marked executing" (cli.rs:773) |
| `cleanup` | "Pass --force to git worktree remove and kill stale runs" (cli.rs:793) |
| `def-done` | "Overwrite generated criteria/helper files" (cli.rs:431) |
| `doc` | "Overwrite existing export or polish output" (cli.rs:848) |

Three distinct meanings of `--force`: (a) escalate process termination, (b) overwrite destination, (c) override safety guard. The user has to remember which command's `--force` is which.

### 5.4 `--quiet` vs `--no-hints` vs `--brief` vs `--plain`

- `run` has `--brief` (single-line preview, cli.rs:480) and `--no-hints` (cli.rs:515).
- `chain` has `--quiet` (cli.rs:592), `--plain` (cli.rs:594), `--no-hints` (cli.rs:590).
- `attach` has `--no-hints` (cli.rs:867).

Four flags trying to suppress different bits of output. None cross-apply.

### 5.5 `--include-manifest` parity

Both `finish` (cli.rs:687) and `materialize` (cli.rs:726) have `--include-manifest`. `apply` does not. This is correct (apply uses git, not file copy) but the user has to know that.

### 5.6 `--branch` semantics

- `run --branch` → "Branch name for worktree runs" (cli.rs:470)
- `chain --branch-policy` → policy enum, not a name (cli.rs:543)
- `finish --branch` → "Apply target branch" (cli.rs:695)
- `apply --branch` → "Target branch" (cli.rs:744)

Three different meanings for `--branch`: source-branch creator, policy enum, target-branch destination.

## 6. Color and style system (non-TUI)

### 6.1 Helpers (`crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:130-205`)

| Helper | ANSI SGR | Semantic intent | Stream |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ui_heading` | `1;36` (bold cyan) | section header | stdout |
| `ui_muted` | `2` (dim) | secondary text | stdout |
| `ui_id` | `1;35` (bold magenta) | run-id / chain-id | stdout |
| `ui_command` | `1;34` (bold blue) | command tokens / hint label | stdout |
| `ui_ok` | `1;32` (bold green) | success | stdout |
| `ui_warn` | `1;33` (bold yellow) | warning | stdout |
| `ui_prompt_prefix` | `1;36` | `?` glyph for prompts | stdout |
| `ui_status(x)` | green if `ok`/`polished` else yellow | mixed status | stdout |
| `ui_error` | `1;31` (bold red) | error label | stderr |
| inline `"hint:"` | `1;34` | hint label | stderr |

### 6.2 Helper coverage drift

Direct `ui_style(text, "1;NN", ...)` calls bypassing helpers exist; these are de facto missing helpers:
- `main.rs:204` — `ui_style("hint:", "1;34", UiStream::Stderr)` — there's no `ui_hint()` helper, code is duplicated.
- `main.rs:4805` — `ui_style(text, "1;31", UiStream::Stdout)` — red bold on **stdout**, not stderr (`ui_error` is stderr-only). Likely an error-themed string written to stdout, breaking the "errors go to stderr in red" rule.
- `main.rs:6626-6627` — `"deadreckoning"` (1;36, cyan) and `course` (1;34, blue) on stderr — these are the run start banner. Both are decoration, but use the ID/heading codes inconsistently.
- `main.rs:7082` — `"changes to apply:"` styled inline (`1;36`) directly rather than via `ui_heading`.
- `main.rs:7218` — `ui_style(...)` direct call.
- `main.rs:12208`, `12378`, `12419`, etc. — TUI styles, expected.

Implied missing helpers: `ui_hint()`, `ui_banner_left()`/`ui_banner_right()`, separate `ui_error_inline()` vs `ui_error_label()`.

### 6.3 `ui_status` is implicit policy

`ui_status` returns green only when the literal status string is `ok` or `polished`. Any other status (including `passed`, `applied`, `completed`, `running`) renders as yellow warning. This means:
- `chain status` row showing `running` looks like a warning.
- A passed gate would be yellow because the literal is `passed`, not `ok`.

### 6.4 NO_COLOR / dumb-terminal honored

`ui_enabled` checks `NO_COLOR` env and `TERM=dumb` (main.rs:137-142). Both `UiStream::Stdout` and `UiStream::Stderr` paths short-circuit when their respective `is_terminal()` is false.

## 8. Output formatting

(Detail from output-audit agent — to be merged.)

### 8.1 Hint policy

`error_hint` (`main.rs:103-128`) maps these error kinds to hints — only those with hints:
- `MissingCredential` / `NoRoute` → suggests `init` or `config set providers.anthropic.api_key`.
- Spend-cap-exceeded → suggests `--i-know-its-a-lot` or lower `--max-spend`.
- `NotFound` → suggests `deadreckon list`.
- `LockHeld` → suggests list / attach / kill.
- `Sandbox` → suggests `doctor`.
- `TomlDe`/`TomlSer` → suggests checking config or `init`.
- `Io` → suggests checking path.
- `Json` → suggests inspecting file.
- `Core(_)` and `Provider(_)` catch-all → **no hint**.

Inconsistency: provider errors other than `MissingCredential`/`NoRoute` (e.g. HTTP errors, rate-limit) get no hint. Core errors that are not the listed three kinds also get no hint. Users hit blank walls.

### 8.2 The hint hardcoded path

`error_hint` returns the literal path `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml` for `TomlDe`/`TomlSer` (`main.rs:122`). This is a **hardcoded home directory**, not the actual `DeadreckonPaths` resolution. On a fresh machine this string is wrong.

## 10. Run lifecycle flows end-to-end

(Detail from lifecycle-audit agent — to be merged.)

### 10.1 State→action map

| State | Visible verbs (what user is told to do) | Hidden verbs that also work |
|---|---|---|
| no runs | `init`, `def-done`, `run` | — |
| `pending`/`planned` | `attach`, `status`, `kill` | `show`, `inspect` |
| `executing` | `attach`, `status`, `kill` | `show`, `inspect` |
| `completed` (worktree) | `finish`, `apply`/`keep`, `attach` (replay), `extend`, `abandon`/`discard` | `show`, `doc`, `library`/`artifacts` |
| `completed` (fresh/copy) | `finish`, `materialize`/`export`/`copy-out`, `extend` | `show`, `doc` |
| `completed` (in-place) | `finish` (shows review guidance), `extend` | `show`, `undo`/`restore` |
| `failed` | `resume`/`continue`, `show`, `kill`/`stop` | `undo`, `cleanup` |
| `killed` | `resume`/`continue`, `cleanup`/`prune`/`clean` | `undo`, `abandon` |

### 10.2 `finish` routing

`FINISH_HELP` (cli.rs:214-225):
\```
worktree run -> apply
fresh/copy run -> export
in-place run -> show review guidance
\```
Three possible side-effects from one command. The first two are physical changes (git apply, fs copy). The third is just a printout. UX inconsistency: a user who runs `finish` on a worktree run does something destructive; the same verb on an in-place run does nothing.

# Deadreckon CLI Output Audit

Scope: `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs` (14,304 lines). The two library crates inspected (`deadreckon-core/src/*.rs`, `deadreckon-providers/src/*.rs`) contain **no user-facing `println!`/`eprintln!`/`writeln!(stdout|stderr)` sites** (the only matches are `writeln!` to a `.gitignore` file in `codebase.rs:456` and string literals inside `smoke.rs`). Libraries are clean.

Total print sites in `main.rs`: **446** (`grep -E 'println!|eprintln!|writeln!'`).

---

## 1. Color/style helper coverage

Helpers defined at `main.rs:130-205`:

| Helper | ANSI code | Stream | Intent | Direct call count |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ui_heading` | `1;36` (cyan bold) | Stdout | Section headers | 46 |
| `ui_muted` | `2` (dim) | Stdout | `hint:` label, `-`, "models:" subtext | 13 |
| `ui_id` | `1;35` (magenta bold) | Stdout | Run/chain/provider IDs | 22 |
| `ui_command` | `1;34` (blue bold) | Stdout | Suggested CLI commands and `try:`/`next:`/`fix:` markers | 119 |
| `ui_ok` | `1;32` (green bold) | Stdout | Success states/checks | 36 |
| `ui_warn` | `1;33` (yellow bold) | Stdout | Warnings and `✗` failure dots | 32 |
| `ui_prompt_prefix` | `1;36` ("?") | Stdout | Confirmation prompt prefix | 2 (definition + prompt fn) |
| `ui_status` | green if `ok`/`polished`, else yellow | Stdout | Polish subcall status | 2 (definition + one use at L9061) |
| `ui_error` | `1;31` (red bold) | Stderr | Top-level `error:` label | 2 (definition + main loop at L202) |

Plus an undeclared "helper" added later:

- `ui_error_stdout(text)` at **`main.rs:4804`** — `ui_style(text, "1;31", UiStream::Stdout)`. Used at **`main.rs:4773`** for the failed-required acceptance mark `✗`. Lives 4 600 lines away from the rest of the helpers and is not referenced in the comment block at the top.

### Inline `ui_style(...)` calls that bypass the helpers

Beyond the helper definitions and the `error_hint` line, six call sites embed raw ANSI codes:

| Line | Code | Where | Why-it-drifts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main.rs:204` | `"1;34"` Stderr | top-level `hint:` label after an error | should be a `ui_hint` helper; bare inline call instead |
| `main.rs:4805` | `"1;31"` Stdout | `ui_error_stdout` body | duplicates `ui_error` semantics on a different stream — missing helper |
| `main.rs:6626` | `"1;36"` Stderr | spinner "deadreckoning" label | duplicates `ui_heading` on Stderr — missing helper |
| `main.rs:6627` | `"1;34"` Stderr | spinner course glyphs | duplicates `ui_command` on Stderr |
| `main.rs:7082` | `"1;36"` Stderr | "changes to apply:" header before diffstat | should be `ui_heading` but routed to stderr |
| `main.rs:7218-7222` | `"1;33"` Stderr | "working tree has uncommitted changes:" warning | should be `ui_warn` but routed to stderr |

So three semantic helpers effectively need stderr variants (`ui_hint`, `ui_heading_err`, `ui_warn_err`) or a single helper that takes a stream argument — the current helpers all hard-wire Stdout even when the call site needs Stderr.

---

## 2. Stdout vs stderr policy

Documented behaviour by command (read from listed sites):

| Output kind | Current routing | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Top-level `error: ...` and trailing `hint: ...` | stderr | `main.rs:202-205` |
| Normal command success (`status`, `list`, `show`, `apply`, `finish`, `chain show`, `chain list`, `library`, `doctor`, `def-done`, `config`, `init`) | stdout | e.g. `8322`, `5328`, `9661`, `7158`, `8660` |
| `cancelled` after user declines a prompt | **stdout** | `1791`, `3262`, `4172`, `7090`, `7412`, `8893`, `10120` |
| Run-completion banner (`completed run`, `paused run`, `killed run`, `failed run`) | stdout | `4284-4287`, `7787-7792`, `9276-9279`, `9098-9100`, `9197` |
| Lifecycle hints (next-actions) | stdout | `9871-9939` |
| Chain attach embedded errors (`error: {err}`) | **stderr** | `2849`, `2860`, `2871`, `2882`, `2834`, `10170`, `10267-10269` |
| Run preview text (`continue?` prompt context) | **stderr** | `4159` (preview), `4169` (preview before prompt) |
| Apply diff stat preview header | **stderr** | `7080-7084` |
| Apply autostash warning + dirty file list | **stderr** | `7216-7228` |
| Stash confirmation note | **stderr** | `7255` ("stashed local changes as ...") |
| Non-git mode chooser (`[1] git init...`) | **stderr** | `6565-6568` |
| Spinner `deadreckoning ...` ticker | stderr | `6611-6630` |
| `prompt(...)` itself (the `? ` and message) | stdout via `print!` | `6578-6584` |

Observations / inconsistencies:

- **`cancelled` is always stdout** (`println!`) even though the action was triggered from a stderr-routed preview/warning. A user redirecting stderr to a log file will lose the warning but keep the `cancelled`. Conversely, the `apply` diff and `autostash` warnings would benefit from being on stdout once the user has confirmed, since they document an action that just happened.
- **`chain attach` error path** prints `error: {err}` raw to stderr (e.g. `main.rs:2849`) — no `ui_error("error:")` styling, unlike the top-level error path (`202`). Same drift at `2834`, `2860`, `2871`, `2882`, `10170`, `10267`. The TUI completion-key handler at `10269` emits a raw `"  hint: {hint}"` to stderr — no muted styling and no ANSI escape. This is at least four parallel hand-rolled error-formatting paths.
- **`acceptance_request_text` prompt text** (`main.rs:4814-4817`) prints plain `"what should count as done? "` via `prompt()` (which uses stdout); fine, but inconsistent with the run-preview/apply confirmations that print preview to stderr and prompt to stdout — confirmation messages are split between two streams in a single user interaction.
- **`note launch-dir is unchanged; completed output lives in artifact`** (`main.rs:9788`) is a neutral informational line printed without any style.
- **No usage of `eprintln!` for ordinary informational text** is wholly wrong, but the policy is inconsistent: most preview/diff/warning text uses stderr, while empty-result hints (`"no runs"`, `"no chains"`, `"no library artifacts ..."`) use stdout.

---

## 3. Color semantics audit

- `ui_ok` is correctly used only for "success-y" outcomes (`completed run`, `applied`, `wrote`, `installed`, `set`, `ready`, `done criteria configured`, the `✓` doctor mark). Consistent.
- `ui_warn` is overloaded: it is used for genuine warnings (`done criteria failed`, `paused run`, `failed run`), but also for clearly **negative/failure** events that read as errors:
  - `main.rs:4286 ui_warn("killed run")` and `4287 ui_warn("failed run")` — `failed run` is not a warning, it is a failure.
  - `7791-7792 ui_warn("killed extended run")`, `ui_warn("failed extended run")` — ditto.
  - `5113 ui_warn("done criteria draft failed")` — failure.
  - `5984, 6012, 6029, 6044, 6072, 6091, 6125, 6132, 6155, 6179, 6193, 6213, 6273` — every doctor failure mark is `ui_warn("✗")`; semantically these are pass/fail dots, not warnings. (Cf. `print_provider_list_row` at `1145-1147` where `ProbeStatus::Failed` also uses `ui_warn("✗")` — same drift.)
- Color drift on the same glyph: `✗` is yellow (`ui_warn`) in doctor and `print_provider_list_row`, but **red** (`ui_error_stdout`) at `main.rs:4773` (failed required acceptance). The `!` mark for optional-failed acceptance at `4775` is `ui_warn`.
- `ui_status` (`main.rs:186`) makes green/yellow conditional only on the literal strings `"ok"` and `"polished"`. Anything else (including `"failed"`, `"error"`, `"timeout"`) gets yellow. So a polish subcall in `failed` state at `9061` renders yellow, not red.
- `eprintln!` plain text that should arguably be styled:
  - `main.rs:2849` `eprintln!("error: {err}")` — no `ui_error`.
  - `main.rs:2834` `eprintln!("selected step has no run yet")` — neutral informational, but printed to stderr unstyled.
  - `main.rs:7225, 7228` — dirty file list rows under a yellow header are unstyled.
  - `main.rs:7255` `eprintln!("stashed local changes as {refname}")` — no `ui_ok` for a successful action.
  - `main.rs:6565-6568` non-git chooser bullets — unstyled stderr.
- `println!("error: ...")`-style: none found outside the routed `ui_error` and the in-TUI `eprintln!("error: ...")` paths.

## 4. Capitalization and punctuation

A lot of drift here, especially around headers.

Header trailing punctuation (cyan `ui_heading` strings):

- With trailing colon:
  - `main.rs:554 "Usage:"`, `557 "Typical flow:"`, `567 "Core lifecycle:"`, `580 "Continue or recover:"`, `590 "More help:"`, `609 "Options:"`, `605 "Note:"`, `9875 "next actions:"`, `9908 "next actions:"`, `7082 "changes to apply:"`, `9050 "doc polish:"`, `7219 "working tree has uncommitted changes:"`.
- Without trailing colon (heading alone):
  - `619 "deadreckon commands"`, `621 "core lifecycle"`, `636 "continue and recover"`, `648 "inspect and advanced"`, `956 "provider selection"`, `1080 "provider registry"`, `1219 "provider detection"`, `5087 "done criteria"`, `5659 "checks"`, `9697 "run health"`, `9721 "library"`, `9742 "disk"`, `5948 "deadreckon doctor"`, `4457 "deadreckon def-done"`, the chain-help blocks `1253, 1264, 1274, 1282, 1289, 1298, 1313, 1326, 1339, 1344`, `8660 "library artifact"`.

Capitalization within `ui_heading`: **Title-case is used for top-level help** (`Usage:`, `Typical flow:`, `Core lifecycle:`) at `554-580` but **lower-case is used everywhere else**, including the parallel `help-all` block 60 lines below (`619 "deadreckon commands"`, `621 "core lifecycle"`, `636 "continue and recover"`). So `print_top_help` and `print_help_all` disagree about case.

`status` header lines mix capitalizations too:

- `show_command` uses `Title Case` for plain labels: `9338 "Extended from {}"`, `9341 "Mode {}"`, `9343 "Branch {branch}"`, `9346 "Worktree {}"`, `9349 "Source {}"`, `9352 "Acceptance {}"`, `9355 "AcceptanceSpec {}"`.
- `print_status` uses `lower-case` and right-aligned colon: `9662 "  run:"`, `9663 "  state:"`, `9665 "  scope:"` and so on through `9709`.
- `print_run_summary` (`9773-9779`) uses lower-case with **no separator at all** — `"status {}"`, `"goal {}"`, `"spend {:.6}"`, `"phase {} {}"`.

So three different "status-like" outputs use three different label conventions.

`print_chain_attach_snapshot` (`main.rs:2770-2804`) uses pipe-delimited single-line headers: `"policy: ... | apply=... | on-fail=... | base=...@..."`; while `chain_show_command` (`main.rs:2718-2733`) uses space-separated key/value `"policy {} apply={} on-fail={} base={}@{}"`. Same data, different formatting.

`print_library_entry` (`main.rs:8660-8678`) uses aligned column with `"run:        "`, `"scope:      "`, `"promoted:   "`, etc. — kebab-case label with colon — but the matching `library list` table header is upper-case (`8607 "RUN\tSCOPE\tPROMOTED\tMATERIALIZED\tPATH\tGOAL"`).

Trailing punctuation in info lines: most lines have no terminal period (`552`, `9882`, `9714`). One exception: `9788 "note launch-dir is unchanged; completed output lives in artifact"` and `9753 "warning:  low disk; clean old worktrees and artifacts soon"` use semicolons mid-line.

"ID" vs "id" vs "Id":

- Columns: `8319 "RUN", "STATUS", "AGE", "SCOPE", "MODE", "ACTION"` and `8628 "RUN", "AGE", "SCOPE", "EXPORTED"` use all-caps.
- Inline messages: `8336 "run ids accept prefixes"`, `8584 "run id prefix {run_id:?}"`, `116 "valid run ids or config keys"` — lowercase `id`.
- Mixed: `2856 "new chain step goal:"` uses lowercase; `9338 "Extended from {marker.parent_run_id}"` uses raw value without a label.

Em-dash vs comma vs colon as separator: not used; the codebase consistently picks `:`, ` ` (single space), or `|`. No em-dash use found.

## 5. Hint blocks

`ui_muted("hint:")` is used at:

- `main.rs:1109` (providers list hint about `--all`)
- `main.rs:8337` (run list table footer)
- `main.rs:8389` (library search no-match)
- `main.rs:8598` (empty library hint)
- `main.rs:8644` (library table footer)

Plain `println!("hint: ...")` without muted styling at:

- `main.rs:7384` `"hint: use \`deadreckon cleanup --completed\` ..."`
- `main.rs:7388` `"hint: use \`deadreckon cleanup --all\` ..."`
- `main.rs:8312` `"hint: use \`deadreckon list --all\` ..."`
- `main.rs:10269` `eprintln!("  hint: {hint}")` (TUI completion-key error path)

The post-top-level-error hint uses **inline `ui_style("hint:", "1;34", Stderr)`** (`main.rs:204`) — bright blue, not muted. So `hint:` shows in **three different visual styles** depending on origin:

| Style | Code | Where |
|---|---|---|
| muted (dim, `2`) | `ui_muted` | empty-state hints in lists/library/providers |
| bright blue bold (`1;34`) | inline `ui_style` | trailing hint after a top-level CLI error |
| unstyled | bare `println!`/`eprintln!` | cleanup empty, list-empty, TUI error |

Two-space indent prefix `"  hint:"` is used only at the top-level error path (`204`) and the TUI completion error (`10269`). Everywhere else hints are flush-left ("hint:" without indent).

`error_hint` paths that do **not** produce a hint and so the user gets no actionable suggestion (see §9 below for the full audit):

- Plain `eprintln!("error: ...")` paths in chain-attach (`2849`, `2860`, `2871`, `2882`) bypass `error_hint` entirely.
- The TUI completion handler at `10267-10270` calls `error_hint` but renders the hint without styling and without the muted/blue convention.

Continue?"` uses a leading flag and capital "Continue"; `4170` is `"continue?"`; `2878` is `"kill chain?"` (verb only); `5090` is `"write done criteria before this {noun}?"` (verb only); `7088` is `"apply these changes?"`; `7313` is `"remove deadreckon worktree and temporary branch now?"`. No `(y/N)` (parens) form is used anywhere — all sites are bracketed.

## 8. Pluralization and units

- **Spend formatting** varies:
  - `${:.6}` in chain show (`2734-2739`), status (`9670`), library, run summary (`9777`).
  - `${:.2}` in `print_chain_attach_snapshot` (`2782-2786`) and the spend-confirmation prompt (`5936`).
  - Doctor doesn't show spend.
  - Chains list table uses `${:<9.6}` (`3640`).
  So the same value appears as `$0.000123` and `$0.00` in different views.
- **Wall time** uses `{:.1}s` (`9678`) and `format_wall_cap` for the cap; the prompt at `5936` calls it `--max-spend is ${max_spend:.2}` (no unit). Acceptance check result elapsed at `4783-4785` uses `"({:.1}s)"`.
- **Bytes/Disk**: `kb / 1024` gives "MB" labels (`6195`, `6206`, `9746`) — there is no GB rollover for the doctor lines.
- **Pluralization**:
  - `materialized_count_label` (`main.rs:8650-8656`): `0 => "no"`, `1 => "yes (1)"`, `n => "yes ({n})"`. Consistent.
  - `chain.steps.len()` is shown raw (`{}/{}`) with no plural word.
  - `print_chain_table` says `STEPS` column unconditionally; `chain_preview` (called at `1762`) says `"  {}. {}", step.index + 1, step.goal` without "step(s)".
  - `print_lifecycle_hints` and "chained: {} done {}/{}" (`2164-2168`) print the same `steps.len()/steps.len()` twice without a word.
  - `"checks: {count}"` and `"  checks:"` in def-done (`4695`, `5659`) — never "1 check" vs "2 checks".
  - `"  pids:     {}"` (`9700`) — no "pid(s)".
  - `print_acceptance_results` uses `"required"` / `"optional"` aligned `{:<8}`; never `requireds`.
- **Currency**: every monetary value uses `$N.NN`. No `USD` suffix anywhere.
- **Percent**: not used in user-facing strings.

## 9. `error_hint` mapping (`main.rs:103-128`)

The hint map covers:

- `Provider::MissingCredential`, `Provider::NoRoute` → init/config hint
- `Core::InvalidInput` containing `"max spend above $50"` → `--i-know-its-a-lot` hint
- `Core::NotFound` → `deadreckon list`
- `Core::LockHeld` → list / attach / kill
- `Sandbox(_)` → `deadreckon doctor`
- `TomlDe`/`TomlSer` → config path with hard-coded `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml`
- `Io(_)`, `Json(_)` → generic "check path"/"inspect JSON"

Variants that return `None`:

1. **`Core::InvalidInput` (any other text)** at the catch-all `Core(_) | Provider(_) => None` branch (line 126). There are 40+ `InvalidInput` user-error sites in `main.rs` that already include hint text in the body (e.g. `4025-4030 "--smoke selects the local scripted provider; omit --provider"`, `4164-4167 "non-interactive without --yes"`, `7094 "non-interactive apply requires --no-confirm"`, `7330 "cannot abandon in-place edits"`). These reach the user only through the error body, not via the styled `hint:` line.
2. **`Provider::*` other than MissingCredential/NoRoute** (e.g. transport, rate-limit, parse errors) all fall through to `None`. There's no hint pointing to `doctor` even though provider transport errors are typical doctor cases.
3. **`Core::LockHeld { .. }` returns a hint, but `Core` lock release errors that are *not* `LockHeld` go to `None`. The struct variants like `LockMismatch` exist in `deadreckon-core/src/error.rs` (not shown here) and may also surface here.
4. The hard-coded path `"/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml"` (line 122) is **a literal user-home string**, not `paths.config_path().display()`. On any other machine this hint is wrong.

The `TomlDe`/`TomlSer` arm hard-codes `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml`; this is a bug for any non-`gdc` user (and would be unhelpful on a host whose `DEADRECKON_HOME` differs).

# Provider Configuration & Management UX Audit — `deadreckon`

Scope: `crates/deadreckon/src/{main.rs,cli.rs}`, `crates/deadreckon-providers/src/{types.rs,config.rs,registry/mod.rs,smoke.rs,taxonomy.rs,error.rs}`, `crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/doctor.rs`, and the tests `providers_list.rs`, `detect.rs`, `registry.rs`, `cli_providers.rs`.

All file refs use absolute paths and line numbers from the current repo (`main.rs` is 14304 lines, on `main`).

---

## 1. Init flow walk-through

`init_command` is `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:823-868`.

Top of the function (every branch hits this first):
1. `paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover()` then `fs::create_dir_all(paths.home())` — **no message**, no check whether `config.toml` already exists.
2. Builds `ProviderRegistry::with_overrides(paths.home())` — silent unless TOML parse fails.

Branch resolution for the provider (`main.rs:835-841`):

| Branch | Output before write | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--provider <id>` supplied | (no echo) | `<id>` is taken verbatim and never validated against the registry. |
| no provider + `--no-confirm` | (no echo) | Calls `auto_subscription_cli_provider(&registry)` (`main.rs:870-883`). Picks **first** subscription CLI in `BTreeMap` order whose `default_binary` is on `PATH`. Falls back to literal string `"anthropic"`. |
| no provider, interactive | `? provider [<detected>]: ` | `prompt_provider()` (`main.rs:6542-6556`). The `<detected>` is computed inline by checking `claude` then `codex` on PATH — **a different rule from `auto_subscription_cli_provider`** (registry vs PATH order). |

`--api-key` branch (`main.rs:842-848`):
- If `api_key` flag was passed → used as-is.
- Else if provider starts with `cli:` → no key needed, no prompt.
- Else → interactive prompt: `? provider API key (leave blank to use env var): `. **Never asks in `--no-confirm` mode** (because `prompt` is `.ok()`-wrapped and stdin will return empty on a non-tty, falling into the empty branch).

Write step (`main.rs:849-857`):
- `init_config_text(...)` (body at `main.rs:6654+`) — composes the TOML body. Always writes both `default_provider` (legacy) and `[defaults] provider/doc_provider` (canonical). `doc_provider` is forced to equal `provider` regardless of CLI flags.
- `fs::write(paths.config_path(), config)?` — **if this fails the user sees the underlying `io::Error` propagated as `CliError::Io`** via the `?`, formatted by the top-level error printer (`ui_error` red on stderr). The `paths.config_path()` is **not** mentioned.
- On success prints (stdout): `<green>wrote</green> /path/to/config.toml` (`main.rs:857`).

Doctor sub-call (`main.rs:858`):
- Always runs `doctor_command().await?` next. The full doctor output (see §3) is appended directly to init's stdout.
- A doctor failure aborts init (because `?`), so the user never sees the final "next:" hint.

Shell-completion branch (`main.rs:859-861`):
- Default (`--no-completion` not set) → `try_install_completion_after_init()` (`main.rs:738-750`).
  - On success the completion installer (`install_completion`, `main.rs:708-736`) prints:
    - `<green>installed</green> completion /path/to/_deadreckon`
    - For zsh + new fpath block: `<green>updated</green> ~/.zshrc`
    - For zsh + pre-existing block: `<green>ready</green> zshrc already loads completion dir`
    - Then: `<blue>next:</blue> <blue>open a new shell, or source your shell rc file</blue>` (`main.rs:730-734`).
  - On failure: stderr `<yellow>note</yellow> shell completion not installed: <err>` then `<blue>try:</blue> <blue>deadreckon completion install --shell zsh</blue>`. **Note color/severity**: this uses `ui_warn("note")` — yellow `note` token — rather than the `✗` symbol used elsewhere.
- `--no-completion` → skipped silently.

Final line (`main.rs:862-866`): `<blue>next:</blue> <blue>deadreckon run "describe the coding task"</blue>`.

Init re-run (config already exists): There is **no detection** — `init_command` silently overwrites `config.toml` with whatever `init_config_text` returns and re-runs doctor on top.

Invalid `--provider <id>` (`init`): writes the value into TOML unchanged and continues. Doctor's `doctor_providers` (`main.rs:6042-6099`) will then loop the `[providers]` table; only `cli:`/`anthropic`/`openai`/etc are recognised, so an invalid id may be classified as either a CLI provider (because the heuristic is `kind.contains("cli") || name.starts_with("cli:")`) or fall through to `provider_has_key` — and emit one of the credential branches. The user is never told the id is invalid.

## 2. Config command surface

Defined in `cli.rs:1073-1102`, dispatched in `main.rs:885-950`.

| Subcommand | Behaviour | Output on success | Output on miss / invalid |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config get <key>` (`main.rs:888-898`) | Reads `config.toml`, traverses dotted key | `<value-to-display>` printed raw (no prefix). For string values: raw string; for everything else: `toml::Value::to_string()` (`main.rs:6772-6777`). | If key missing: returns `CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::NotFound("config key <key>"))`. Surfaces as red stderr `<red>error</red>: not found: config key <key>` (or the project's standard error template — see top-level error printer). |
| `config set <key> <value>` (`main.rs:899-905`) | Writes value via `set_toml_path`. Value parsing in `parse_config_value` (`main.rs:6765-6770`) tries TOML first, falls back to literal string. **Never validates** that the key is a known field. | `<green>set</green> <key>` | Unknown / mistyped key: **succeeds silently** and writes the value to whatever path was given. |
| `config provider` (no arg) (`main.rs:923`) | Falls through to `print_provider_selection(&paths, None)` (see below). | See "provider selection" block in §5. | Config file missing → `print_provider_selection` calls `ProviderRouter::from_config_path`. Empty config → empty list → only the heading is printed; no "try:" hints. |
| `config provider <id>` (`main.rs:907-922`) | Writes both `defaults.provider` and `default_provider` (legacy). | `<green>set</green> default provider <magenta>cli:codex</magenta>` | No validation against registry; any string is accepted. |
| `config model` (no arg) (`main.rs:946`) | `print_provider_selection(&paths, provider.as_deref())` | See §5. | — |
| `config model <model>` (`main.rs:925-945`) | Requires an `active_provider` (either `--provider` flag or read from `defaults.provider`/`default_provider`). | `<green>set</green> model for <magenta>cli:codex</magenta> -> <magenta>gpt-5.1-codex</magenta>` | No active provider: returns `CliError::Core(user_error("no active provider configured", "deadreckon config provider cli:codex"))` — formatted with a "try" hint by the top-level renderer. |

Notable: **there is no `config list`, `config show`, `config unset`, or `config delete` subcommand** despite `CONFIG_HELP` advertising `deadreckon config get/set/provider/model`. The visible alias is `settings` (`cli.rs:378`).

`config get`'s output for a missing parent path: `get_toml_path` (`main.rs:6733-6739`) returns `None` for any intermediate miss — so `defaults.does_not_exist`, `does_not_exist.foo` both produce the same `NotFound("config key ...")` shape.

`config get` for nested table value (e.g. `config get providers`): prints the TOML inline-table representation via `toml::Value::to_string()` — not the pretty form. This will surprise users who expect `[providers] ...` headers.

| provider ping (only when `DEADRECKON_DOCTOR_PING=1`) | `✓`/`✗` | green / yellow | `✓ provider anthropic ping ok model claude-sonnet-4-5 \| try: deadreckon run "goal" --provider anthropic --preview` or `✗ provider anthropic ping failed` + `    fix: check credentials or set a fallback provider (<err>)` or `✗ provider anthropic ping timed out` + `    fix: check network/provider status or unset DEADRECKON_DOCTOR_PING` | `main.rs:6101-6140` |
| default provider summary | `✓` or `✗` | green / yellow | `✓ provider defaults configured \| try: deadreckon config provider`, or `✓ cli subscription provider available \| try: deadreckon init --no-confirm`, or `✗ no provider configured` + `    fix: deadreckon init or deadreckon config set providers.anthropic.api_key <KEY>` | `main.rs:6015-6034` |
| disk + permissions | `✓` writable / `✗` unwritable or low disk | green / yellow | `✓ runstate dir /Users/gdc/.deadreckon/runstate writable \| try: deadreckon run "goal" --preview`, `✗ runstate dir ... not writable` + `    fix: chmod u+w ...` + `    detail: <err>`, `✗ disk space low: 100 MB free in ...` + `    fix: free at least 1 GB or set DEADRECKON_HOME to a larger disk`, `✓ disk space 4096 MB free in ... \| try: deadreckon status` | `main.rs:6154-6225` |
| OS | `✓` | green | `✓ os macOS 15.6.1 \| try: sw_vers -productVersion` / `✓ os Linux kernel 6.5 \| try: uname -r` | `main.rs:6227-6256` |
| subscription binaries (`claude`, `codex` only) | `✓`/`✗` | green / yellow | `✓ subscription binary claude 1.0 (Claude Code) \| try: deadreckon config provider cli:claude-code` or `✗ subscription binary claude missing` + `    fix: install claude or choose another provider with \`deadreckon config set defaults.provider <name>\`` | `main.rs:6258-6279`. **Always runs even if user is already on `cli:codex`, so a working setup still shows `✗ subscription binary claude missing` as a yellow ✗.** Also hardcodes `claude` and `codex` only; ignores `cli:gemini`, `cli:opencode`, `cli:copilot`, `cli:pi`. |

Glyph/colour conventions:

- "PASS" is `<green>✓</green>`. There is no separate "WARN" tier — anything not-OK uses `<yellow>✗</yellow>` (same glyph for "fail" and "warn").
- `ui_muted("-")` (dim `-`) appears as a third tier in `providers list`/`detect` but not in `doctor`.
- Fix hints are indented 4 spaces and prefixed with `<blue>fix:</blue>` (an indented continuation line).
- Try hints are inline after `|` and prefixed with `<blue>try:</blue>`.
- Doctor mixes the two styles: passes use `<text> | try: <cmd>` inline; failures use a new indented line `    fix: <cmd>`.

The sandbox / provider / disk checks all render in the same `✓`/`✗ ... |/fix:` skeleton, so they look similar, but the precise format is per-call printf — there is no shared `print_doctor_row` helper.

## 4. Detect output

`detect_command` (`main.rs:1037-1062`) and `print_detect_results` (`main.rs:1218-1247`). Underlying probe data is `ProviderProbeResult` (`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/registry/mod.rs:230-245`).

### 4a. Human output

Header: `<cyan>provider detection</cyan>` (`main.rs:1219`).

Per provider one row:
```
<id-magenta>                <symbol>  <credential>     <location>                            <version>           <metering>
```
Format string (`main.rs:1229-1237`):
```
"{:<20} {}  {:<14} {:<36} {:<18} {}"
   ui_id    sym  credential  location          version        metering
```

- `<symbol>` is one of `<green>✓</green>` / `<yellow>✗</yellow>` / `<dim>-</dim>` from `ProbeStatus::{Ok, Failed, Skipped}` (`main.rs:1221-1225`).
- `credential` is the raw string from `ProviderProbeResult.credential`: `"ready"`, `"missing"`, or `"unknown"` (set in `crates/deadreckon-providers/src/registry/mod.rs:367-489` etc.).
- `location` defaults to `"-"` if `None`.
- `version` defaults to `"-"` if `None`. For HTTP non-`--ping` it is the literal string `"ping skipped"` (`registry/mod.rs:529`). For `LocalHttp` non-`--ping` it is `"ping required"` (`registry/mod.rs:547`). For ping responses it is `"HTTP 200"` etc. (`registry/mod.rs:578`).
- `metering` is `"subscription"` if `descriptor.subscription`, else `"metered"` (`registry/mod.rs:613-617`).
- The columns are not labelled (the human reader has to know that the 3rd column is credential and 4th is location).

If `result.message` is non-empty: indented dim line `    <message-dim>` (`main.rs:1238-1240`).

If `result.status == Failed`: each install-hint `try_line` printed as `    <blue>try:</blue> <blue>line</blue>` (`main.rs:1241-1245`). **For `Skipped` (LocalHttp default) the message is printed but no try-lines.** **For `Ok` no try-lines either, even if `try_lines` is populated.**

### 4b. JSON output (`--json`)

Output (`main.rs:1053-1057`):
```json
{ "providers": [ { ... ProviderProbeResult ... }, ... ] }
```

`ProviderProbeResult` field names (`registry/mod.rs:230-245`):
- `id`, `display_name`, `kind`, `status`, `location`, `version`, `credential`, `subscription`, `metering`, `fs_artifacts`, `error_kind`, `message`, `try_lines`.

`kind` enum labels — `DescriptorKind` is `#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]` (`registry/mod.rs:51-59`):
- `Http` → `"http"`
- `Cli` → `"cli"`
- `LocalHttp` → `"local-http"`
- `Scripted` → `"scripted"`

The CLI helper `descriptor_kind_label` (`main.rs:1209-1216`) hard-codes the same strings. This is **duplicated** rather than reused from serde — risk of drift.

`status` enum (`registry/mod.rs:211-217`): `snake_case` → `"ok"`, `"failed"`, `"skipped"`.

`error_kind` enum (`registry/mod.rs:219-228`): snake_case → `"not_found"`, `"permission_denied"`, `"version_mismatch"`, `"auth_missing"`, `"endpoint_unreachable"`, `"probe_failed"`.

### 4c. Credential-probe vs `--ping` differences

For `Http` providers (`registry/mod.rs:490-534`):
- Without `--ping`: if `auth.kind == ApiKey`, env var is checked (and "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY missing" message produced on miss); otherwise the probe is always `Ok` with `version="ping skipped"`. The credential field is `"ready"` regardless of whether the env var was actually verified to be a real key — only its presence is checked.
- With `--ping`: skips the env-var check **(probably a bug; if no env var, ping happens anyway against the public endpoint)** — actually wait: re-reading lines 494-521, the env-var check runs first and returns early on miss; only if it passes does ping run. OK.

For `LocalHttp` providers (`registry/mod.rs:536-552`):
- Without `--ping`: status is `Skipped` (not `Ok`), credential `"unknown"`, message `"local endpoint probe skipped; pass --ping"`.
- With `--ping`: same endpoint ping as HTTP.

Inconsistency: HTTP without `--ping` returns `status="ok"` whereas LocalHTTP returns `status="skipped"`, even though both did the same amount of work (i.e., none). The `version` field differs (`"ping skipped"` vs `"ping required"`) which is more accurate, but the status field is misleading.

For `Cli` providers (`registry/mod.rs:374-488`): The `--ping` flag is **ignored** — version-probe runs whenever `version_probe.args` is non-empty, regardless of the flag. So `deadreckon detect cli:codex --ping` is no different from `deadreckon detect cli:codex`.

For `Scripted` (`registry/mod.rs:362-371`): always `status=Ok`, `location="built-in"`, `credential="ready"`. `--ping` ignored.

### 4d. `detect <id>` with id that doesn't exist (`main.rs:1041-1048`)

Returns `CliError::Core(user_error("no provider '<id>' in registry", "deadreckon providers list"))`. Rendered on stderr in red via the top-level error printer.

## 5. Providers list output

`providers_list_command` (`main.rs:1072-1114`) + `print_provider_list_row` (`main.rs:1139-1177`) + `print_provider_models` (`main.rs:1179-1207`).

### 5a. Ordering and which providers are shown

Header: `<cyan>provider registry</cyan>` (`main.rs:1080`).

ID selection (`main.rs:1075-1079`):
- Default: `configured_provider_ids(&paths)` (`main.rs:1116-1131`). This reads `read_config` and concatenates `default_provider` then `fallback` then keys of `[providers]`, deduped (insertion order).
- `--all`: `registry.ids()` (alphabetical, `BTreeMap` order).

Empty case (`main.rs:1081-1089`): `<dim>-</dim> no configured providers` then `<blue>try:</blue> <blue>deadreckon providers list --all</blue>`.

Unknown configured id (in config but not in registry) (`main.rs:1090-1098`): `<yellow>✗</yellow> <magenta><id></magenta> not registered | <blue>deadreckon detect</blue>`. This is the **only** place where "not registered" surfaces.

Footer (when **not** `--all`) (`main.rs:1106-1112`): `<dim>hint:</dim> <blue>deadreckon providers list --all</blue>`.

### 5b. Row layout

Default (compact, `main.rs:1164-1176`):
```
{:<20}    <symbol>  {:<10} credential={:<8} model=<model> metering=<metering> location=<loc> version=<ver>
ui_id        ✓/✗/-   kind                       
```
Note: the **width-20 column is the ANSI-coloured `ui_id(...)`** which means the actual byte-width (with escape codes) blows past 20, so the column alignment only works when colors are disabled.

`--full` (`main.rs:1152-1163`):
```
<symbol> <magenta-id> kind=<kind> credential=<cred> model=<model> metering=<met> location=<loc> version=<ver>
```
Same fields, no fixed widths, intended for scripting (the `providers_list_full_emits_exact_paths_no_truncation` test relies on this).

`--models` (`main.rs:1102-1104` → `print_provider_models`, `main.rs:1179-1207`): adds an indented `models:` sub-section per provider:
```
    <dim>models:</dim>
      <magenta-id> aliases=<aliases> context=<n|-> price=$<in>/$<out> per 1M | -
```
- `aliases`: comma-joined or `"-"`.
- `context`: `model.context_window` or `"-"`.
- `price`: only emitted when **both** `input_per_million` and `output_per_million` are `Some`, else `"-"`. Half-priced models get `"-"`.

If catalog is empty: `    <dim>models: none</dim>` (`main.rs:1180-1183`).

### 5c. "Current" indicator

There is **no `*` or `✓` "currently configured" indicator in `providers list`**. The status symbol is per-probe (ready/missing/skipped), not "is the default". Compare with `print_provider_selection` (`main.rs:952-997`) which uses `"*"` for the selected route and a literal space `" "` for unselected — those two surfaces use different conventions for "the active one":

| Surface | "current" marker | "available" marker |
|---|---|---|
| `providers list` | none | `✓` / `✗` / `-` |
| `config provider` / `config model` (no arg) → `print_provider_selection` | `*` for selected, `" "` for others | `credential=ready` / `credential=missing` string |
| `doctor` | uses the existence of `[providers]` entries — no "current" marker | `✓` / `✗` |

### 5d. `auto_subscription_cli_provider` (`main.rs:870-883`)

Recommendation logic for the implicit init path:
1. Iterate the registry (BTreeMap alphabetical).
2. Keep only descriptors where `kind == Cli` AND `subscription == true` AND `default_binary` is non-`None` AND `provider_binary_available(binary)`.
3. Return the first one's `id`.
4. Fallback to `"anthropic"` (literally that string, even though `anthropic` is not a CLI subscription).

Because the registry is alphabetic, the resolution order is:
`cli:claude-code` → `cli:codex` → `cli:copilot` → `cli:gemini` → `cli:opencode` → `cli:pi`.

So with **all** subscription CLIs installed, the user always gets `cli:claude-code`, never `cli:codex`. Test `init_yes_prefers_registry_cli_binary_order` (`tests/detect.rs:104-170`) codifies this. **Inconsistent with `prompt_provider`** which prefers `claude` over `codex` over `anthropic` regardless of registry contents.

### 5e. CLI vs HTTP vs scripted rendering

All providers render with **the same field set** (`kind, credential, model, metering, location, version`). However:

- For CLI providers: `model = descriptor.default_model` which is `None` for cli-claude-code/codex (see `config.rs:64-73` — CLI providers explicitly null out `default_model`). So `providers list` shows `model=-` for the registry-side descriptor.
- For HTTP providers: `model = descriptor.default_model` which is e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`.
- `location` for CLI: filesystem path or `"-"` if not on PATH. For HTTP: the `default_endpoint` URL. Mixing paths and URLs in the same column is acknowledged but unlabelled.
- `version` for HTTP: literally `"ping skipped"` by default — that's not a version, it's a status sentinel.

`metering="subscription"` is set from `descriptor.subscription` which is **only** true for `cli:claude-code`, `cli:codex`, `cli:gemini`, `cli:opencode`, `cli:copilot`, `cli:pi`. Everything else is `"metered"`, including `smoke` which is locally scripted and free.

## 6. Provider terminology

| Term | Where it surfaces publicly | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **provider** | Everywhere — flag names, config keys, help text, output. | The most common term. Configured `[providers.X]` table entries; CLI flag `--provider`; the `provider` field in JSON output. |
| **route** | `provider selection` heading (`main.rs:956`), `selected_route_info()`/`route_info()` (router public API), the `try:` hint `deadreckon run "goal" --provider <name>` is described as "provider route" in `INIT_HELP` line `cli.rs:67` ("`deadreckon config provider`"), in `DETECT_HELP` ("Provider route override"), in `RUN_HELP`, and in `Init`/`Done`/`Run`/`Chain`/`Extend` clap help strings ("Provider route override", "Default provider route", "Provider route to make default"). | In code: an entry in the router's resolved chain (one provider + its config). In help: synonym for "provider id". |
| **model** | `--model` flag, `[providers.X].model` config key, `config model` subcommand, `print_provider_models`, `descriptor.model_catalog`. | A model name within a provider. |
| **descriptor** | `descriptor_kind_label` (`main.rs:1209-1216`), `ProviderDescriptor` (`registry/mod.rs:172-193`), `providers list` heading is `"provider registry"`, `PROVIDERS_HELP` line `cli.rs:99-100` ("registry-backed", "every built-in and override descriptor"), `DETECT_HELP` line `cli.rs:88` ("registered providers from descriptor data"). | Internal data structure. User-facing only in `PROVIDERS_HELP`/`DETECT_HELP`. |
| **kind** | `--kind`? (no — only on `doc`); JSON field `kind`; human row `kind=cli`. Config key `[providers.X].kind`. `ProviderKind` enum (`types.rs:17-26`) and `DescriptorKind` enum (`registry/mod.rs:53-59`) are **distinct** enums with overlapping but different string vocabularies. | The category of a provider/descriptor. |
| **registry** | Heading `"provider registry"` (`main.rs:1080`), help text "descriptor registry" (`cli.rs:1106`), `PROVIDERS_HELP` ("registry-backed"). | The collection of all descriptors. |
| **route** vs **provider** in help: e.g. `Run.provider` arg help is "Provider route override" (`cli.rs:490`), but `Done.provider` is "Provider route override for drafting" (`cli.rs:426`), while `Init.provider` is "Default provider route, for example cli:codex or cli:claude-code" (`cli.rs:360`). User sees both terms used for the same thing. |

`ProviderKind` enum string set (`types.rs:29-39`): `anthropic`, `open-ai`, `open-ai-compatible`, `cli-claude-code`, `cli-codex`, `scripted-smoke`, plus arbitrary `Generic(id)`.

`DescriptorKind` enum string set: `http`, `cli`, `local-http`, `scripted` (kebab-case via serde).

`format_provider_kind` (`main.rs:1033-1035`) uses `ProviderKind::as_config_str()` — emits the dashed style (`cli-codex`). `descriptor_kind_label` (`main.rs:1209-1216`) uses `DescriptorKind` — emits short form (`cli`). **Same word ("kind") in column headers refers to two different enums depending on the surface.**

Example divergence:
- `provider selection` row (`config provider` / `config model` no arg, via `print_provider_selection`): `kind=cli-codex` (from `ProviderKind`).
- `providers list` row: `kind=cli` (from `DescriptorKind`).
- `detect` JSON: `"kind": "cli"` (from `DescriptorKind`).

## 7. Setup-vs-management language

Visible boundaries (`cli.rs`):
- `Init` (`cli.rs:354`): "Create ~/.deadreckon/config.toml and check the local setup" — about-text. `next_help_heading = "Setup"`, visible alias `setup`.
- `Config` (`cli.rs:379`): "Read or update ~/.deadreckon/config.toml". Alias `settings`.
- `Doctor` (`cli.rs:625`): "Check providers, sandboxing, disk, and local prerequisites". Alias `check`.
- `Detect` (`cli.rs:631`): "Probe registered providers from descriptor data".
- `Providers` (`cli.rs:644`): "List registered provider descriptors".

All five live under the `Setup` help heading.

Same data, different surface:

| Data point | Init prints… | Config prints… | Doctor prints… | Detect prints… | Providers list prints… |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Default provider id | (writes to TOML, no echo) | `<green>set</green> default provider <magenta>X</magenta>` or `* <magenta>X</magenta> ...` inside "provider selection" block | `✓ provider defaults configured` (without saying which one!) | `<id> <symbol> ...` for every registered provider; default not marked | every configured id; default first because of insertion order, but not marked |
| Whether provider has credential | (silently writes `api_key` or `api_key_env`) | `credential=ready/missing` in `print_provider_selection` | `✓ provider X credential present; ping skipped` or `✗ provider X credential missing` | `<symbol>` + `credential=ready/missing` + optional `<env> missing` message | `credential=ready/missing` (post-probe) |
| Whether CLI binary is on PATH | indirectly via doctor sub-call | not surfaced | `✓ provider X CLI binary <binary> found` / `✗ ... missing` | `location=/path/to/bin` + version | `location=...` + version |
| Model defaults | written to config (`doc_provider` ditto) | `model=<m>` in selection | not shown | not shown directly (only via JSON `default_model` which **is not in `ProviderProbeResult`** — it's omitted) | `model=<m>` in row; `--models` adds catalog |

The user crossing from `init` (writes credentials silently) to `doctor` (announces them) to `detect` (probes them via env-var) sees the **same credential** described as: nothing → `credential present` → `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY missing` → `credential=ready` — four different phrasings.

Likewise "provider chosen by `init --no-confirm`" vs "default provider per config" vs "selected route" vs "first id in `providers list`" can all be the same value but never share a marker symbol.

---

## 8. JSON vs human output

The only command with `--json` in scope is `detect`. Confirmed field-level overlap:

| JSON field | Human-print column | Match? |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | first column (magenta) | ✓ |
| `display_name` | **not shown in human output** | ✗ — JSON-only. |
| `kind` (`http`/`cli`/`local-http`/`scripted`) | not shown in `print_detect_results`; shown only in `providers list` row | partial. Human `detect` omits kind entirely. |
| `status` (`ok`/`failed`/`skipped`) | rendered as glyph `✓/✗/-` (no string) | shape match, label drop. |
| `location` | column 4 | ✓ |
| `version` | column 5 | ✓ |
| `credential` (`ready`/`missing`/`unknown`) | column 3 | ✓ |
| `subscription` (bool) | **not shown** | ✗ — JSON-only. |
| `metering` (`subscription`/`metered`) | column 6 | ✓ |
| `fs_artifacts` | **not shown** | ✗ — JSON-only. |
| `error_kind` (`not_found`/…) | **not shown** | ✗ — only the human-readable `message` shows. |
| `message` | indented dim line (when present) | ✓ |
| `try_lines` | indented `try:` lines (only when `status == Failed`) | partial — JSON includes them always; human prints only on failure. |

Other commands have no `--json`:

- `providers list`: no `--json`. The `--full` flag is shell-friendly but still uses human format with `key=value` tokens.
- `config get`: prints raw value with no JSON option. For tables/arrays, the inline-TOML serialisation may not round-trip into a script.
- `config show` / `config list`: don't exist.
- `doctor`: no `--json`. The doctor section names ("source", "home", "sandbox bwrap", "provider X", "disk space", "os", "subscription binary X") aren't machine-readable; only the embedded paths/versions can be parsed.

---

## 9. Error states

**Run init twice (config exists).** `init_command` (`main.rs:823-868`) does not check existence. It silently overwrites `config.toml`. The user sees only the normal flow:
```
✓ wrote /Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml
<doctor output for the new config>
✓ installed completion ...
✓ next: deadreckon run "describe the coding task"
```
There is no "already configured", no confirmation prompt, and no backup. (Compare `init_yes_prefers_registry_cli_binary_order` in `tests/detect.rs:104-170` which exercises an over-write path without any "already exists" assertion.)

**`init --api-key` supplied but `--provider` invalid.** Example: `deadreckon init --provider made-up --api-key abc --no-confirm`. `init_command` (`main.rs:835-848`) takes `provider = "made-up"`; because it doesn't start with `cli:` and `no_confirm` is set, the `--api-key abc` is kept. `init_config_text` (`main.rs:6654-6720`) hits the `_ =>` default branch (`main.rs:6711`) and writes:
```toml
default_provider = "made-up"
fallback = ["anthropic", "openai", "cli:claude-code", "cli:codex"]
...
[providers.anthropic]
kind = "anthropic"
api_key = "abc"
```
i.e. the api-key goes to the `anthropic` block, **not** to `made-up`, because the default arm hard-codes `anthropic`. User sees no error. Doctor afterwards will likely say `✗ provider made-up credential missing` (because there's no `[providers.made-up]`), plus `✓ provider anthropic credential present; ping skipped`. The flag silently wired the key to the wrong provider.

**`config set` with unknown key.** `set_toml_path` (`main.rs:6741-6763`) creates missing tables on the way down. No validation. The user sees:
```
✓ set foo.bar
```
and the value is written verbatim. There is no warning that `foo.bar` is not a recognised config field.

**Doctor finds a missing sandbox backend.** Iteration is over all backends from `deadreckon_sandbox::doctor()`. For a missing one:
```
✗ sandbox bwrap missing
    fix: install bubblewrap (bwrap) for Linux native sandboxing
```
The `note` string comes from `missing_hint` in `crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/doctor.rs:46-55`. On macOS this still prints `✗ sandbox bwrap missing` and `✗ sandbox docker missing` even though they don't apply to that platform, which inflates the failure count.

**`detect <id>` with id that doesn't exist.** `main.rs:1042-1048`. The user gets a `CliError::Core(user_error("no provider '<id>' in registry", "deadreckon providers list"))`. The top-level error printer renders it (red `error:` on stderr) plus a `try: deadreckon providers list` hint. The successful headings ("provider detection") are **not** printed for this case — clean abort.

**`providers list` with no configured providers.** `main.rs:1081-1089`:
```
provider registry      (cyan heading)
- no configured providers          (dim "-")
try: deadreckon providers list --all
```
No status glyph, no row format. Default-list emptiness ≠ `--all` emptiness (which would never happen because the registry is non-empty).

**`config get` with missing key.** Returns `CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::NotFound("config key <key>"))` (`main.rs:891-895`). Rendered as red stderr — no recovery hint, just the not-found message.

**`config model <model>` with no active provider configured.** Returns `CliError::Core(user_error("no active provider configured", "deadreckon config provider cli:codex"))` (`main.rs:929-936`). Has the try hint.

**Detect with `--ping` against a CLI provider.** `--ping` is silently ignored (see §4c). The user has no signal that the flag was effectively a no-op.

**Detect with `--ping` against unreachable HTTP endpoint.** Status `failed`, `error_kind="endpoint_unreachable"` (test `detect_ping_flag_required_for_http_endpoint_probe` codifies this, `tests/detect.rs:317-356`). Human form prints `<provider>  ✗  ready  http://...  -  metered` then `    <dim><reqwest err>...` then `    try: <install hint>`. The `try` lines are install hints, which are **wrong help** for "endpoint unreachable" — install hints are install instructions, not connectivity diagnostics.

---

## Inconsistencies

- `print_provider_list_row` uses `descriptor_kind_label` ("cli", "http", …, `main.rs:1157,1169`) while `print_provider_selection` uses `format_provider_kind` → `ProviderKind::as_config_str` ("cli-codex", "open-ai", …, `main.rs:974`). Same `kind=` token, two different vocabularies.
- "Current"/"active" provider marker differs: `*` in `print_provider_selection` (`main.rs:958-965`); no marker at all in `print_provider_list_row` (`main.rs:1139-1177`); not surfaced in `doctor` (`main.rs:5946-6040`).
- `auto_subscription_cli_provider` (`main.rs:870-883`) picks registry-alphabetical first match; `prompt_provider` (`main.rs:6542-6556`) picks `claude` → `codex` → `anthropic` by PATH check. Same role, different orderings.
- `init_command` overwrites `config.toml` without confirmation; `deadreckon acceptance init` (`main.rs:4521`) refuses with `acceptance.yaml already exists`. Same lifecycle verb, opposite policies.
- `init_command` writes both `default_provider` (top-level legacy) and `defaults.provider` (nested) (`main.rs:6676-6677` and `config provider <id>` at `main.rs:909-919`). `config get defaults.provider` and `config get default_provider` are both valid; `config provider <id>` sets both; **but `config set default_provider X` only sets the legacy one** — and `config_defaults` (`main.rs:5820-5823`) reads `defaults.provider` first, falls back to `default_provider`, so writes to only `default_provider` may be silently shadowed by a stale `defaults.provider`.
- `doctor`'s "source" line hard-codes `/Users/gdc/deadreckon` (`main.rs:5949-5953`) — not a user-relevant path on any other machine.
- `doctor_subscription_binary` is called unconditionally for `claude` and `codex` (`main.rs:6037-6038`), even when the user has chosen e.g. `cli:gemini` or `cli:copilot`. Failing rows for unused binaries are noise.
- `doctor` does not call any provider in `cli:gemini`/`cli:opencode`/`cli:copilot`/`cli:pi` despite them being in the registry; only `claude` and `codex` get the trailing subscription-binary block.
- `DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH` in `providers/src/config.rs:8` is `"/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml"` — committed user-specific absolute path constant.
- HTTP descriptor without `--ping`: `status="ok"` and `version="ping skipped"` (`registry/mod.rs:525-533`). LocalHTTP without `--ping`: `status="skipped"` and `version="ping required"` (`registry/mod.rs:543-552`). Same observation ("we didn't actually contact the endpoint") encoded as two different statuses.
- CLI providers ignore `--ping` (`registry/mod.rs:358-359`). The flag's help — `"Probe HTTP/local endpoints instead of only credentials"` (`cli.rs:639-640`) — is accurate but the user has no way to tell whether `--ping` had any effect on a given row.
- `print_detect_results` (`main.rs:1218-1247`) emits `try_lines` only when `result.status == ProbeStatus::Failed`. The JSON output emits `try_lines` always. Same data, different gating per surface.
- `print_detect_results` columns are unlabelled (`main.rs:1229-1237`); `print_provider_list_row` uses inline `key=value` tokens (`main.rs:1153-1175`). Two adjacent commands that share most fields render them with two different conventions.
- `ProviderKind` (`types.rs:17-26`) and `DescriptorKind` (`registry/mod.rs:53-59`) are duplicated taxonomies. `ProviderKind` includes specific brands (`Anthropic`, `OpenAi`, `CliClaudeCode`, …); `DescriptorKind` includes transport categories (`Http`, `Cli`, `LocalHttp`, `Scripted`). Both surface as `kind=` in user output.
- `ProviderKind::deserialize` accepts dual names (`"openai"` and `"open-ai"`, `"cli:codex"` and `"cli-codex"`, `types.rs:51-67`) but `as_config_str()` only emits the dashed form. So `config get providers.openai.kind` may return `"open-ai"` even though the user wrote `"openai"`. (Also: `Anthropic`'s string is `"anthropic"` not `"anth-ropic"` — the inconsistency between hyphenation styles is internal to the enum.)
- `print_provider_list_row` (default mode) fixed-widths a magenta-coloured `ui_id(...)` to 20 chars (`main.rs:1166-1167`) — Rust's `{:<20}` counts bytes, not display width, so the ANSI escape sequences push the visible column past 20 on a colour terminal.
- `provider_binary_available` (`main.rs:6808-6810`) checks `command_exists || PathBuf::exists` (handles configured absolute paths). `command_exists` (`main.rs:6798-6806`) walks `$PATH`. `prompt_provider` (`main.rs:6542-6549`) uses only `command_exists` (no absolute-path branch). So `init` interactively suggests `anthropic` even if the user configured `[providers."cli:codex"].binary = "/opt/codex/bin/codex"` and that file exists.
- `auto_subscription_cli_provider` fallback returns the literal string `"anthropic"` (`main.rs:838`), but `anthropic` is not a CLI subscription provider — the function name promises one thing and the fallback delivers a different category. Then `init_config_text` honours the string as if it were a regular provider id.
- `init_config_text` (`main.rs:6711-6718`) treats every unknown provider as `anthropic` — including arbitrary user-supplied `--provider made-up`. The user's chosen provider id is written into `default_provider` and `fallback` but the `[providers.<id>]` block is silently substituted to `[providers.anthropic]`. (See §9 "init partial".)
- `print_provider_selection` (`main.rs:952-997`) emits `try:` and `default model:` hints **only when `selected` is `Some`**, but `routes` may be non-empty without a selection (e.g. config sets `default_provider` to a non-existent route). The user would see the route list with no `*` marker and no hints — no clear remediation path.
- `INIT_HELP` (`cli.rs:61-67`) tells the user "Use `deadreckon config provider`" but `print_provider_selection` (which `config provider` invokes when called with no arg) prints `try: deadreckon run ...` instead of acknowledging the user is in a config flow. The mid-flow hint cross-jumps to "Run Lifecycle".
- `CONFIG_HELP` (`cli.rs:69-79`) advertises four subcommands (`get`, `set`, `provider`, `model`). There is no `show`, `list`, `unset`, or `validate`, so a user looking for a roll-up has to use `cat ~/.deadreckon/config.toml` or `config get` for each key.
- `Init` clap arg `--provider` help: `"Default provider route, for example cli:codex or cli:claude-code"` (`cli.rs:360`). `Config provider` clap arg `--provider`: `"Provider route to make default, for example cli:codex"` (`cli.rs:1089`). `Run`'s `--provider`: `"Provider route override"` (`cli.rs:491`). Three different phrasings for the same conceptual argument.
- `detect_command` and `providers_list_command` both load `ProviderRegistry::with_overrides(paths.home())` (`main.rs:1039, 1074`). `init_command` does it too (`main.rs:834`). But `doctor` does **not** use the registry — `doctor_providers` (`main.rs:6042-6098`) walks the `[providers]` TOML table by name and uses string heuristics (`name.contains("claude")` to pick the binary) instead. So a registered descriptor like `cli:gemini` will be tagged with the wrong binary by doctor.
- `try:` hints throughout doctor are colourised twice in some lines (the prefix and the command), but in `detect` the `try:` block is also double-coloured, while `providers list`'s "hint:"/"try:" footer at `main.rs:1108-1112` is `<dim>hint:</dim> <blue>cmd</blue>` — inconsistent colouring of the same conceptual block.
- `ui_warn` is used for the **success** word `"note"` in `try_install_completion_after_init` (`main.rs:742`) — yellow `note` in a non-error context, the only place `ui_warn` is used for non-failure copy.

# Deadreckon Run Lifecycle UX Audit

## Section A — State machine

### Per-run states (`RunStatus`) — `crates/deadreckon-core/src/state.rs:19-42`

| Enum variant | Stored text | CLI text in `status`/`list`/`show` | TUI text | Transitions out (command, observed wording) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Pending` | `pending` | `state: pending -> attach` (`main.rs:9663,8720`); `list` column shows `pending` (`main.rs:8327`) | TUI header from `attach_header_text` `main.rs:12248`; footer states defined in `footer_for_state` `main.rs:12278` | `run_command` advances to `Planned` during init (`create_run` sets phase id 0 to Planned at `state.rs:234`); user sees nothing per-state. |
| `Planned` | `planned` | same as above with `-> attach` | same | Set by `set_phase_status(_,Planned)` (`state.rs:169`); `run_command` then moves to Executing. |
| `Executing` | `executing` | `state: executing -> attach` (`main.rs:8720`), or `-> cleanup --stale` if `is_stale_executing` (`main.rs:8717`) | live TUI rendered by `attach_tui` (`main.rs:10123`+) | `kill_command` → `Killed` (prints `killed run <id>` or `killed run <id> forcefully`, `main.rs:9098-9101`); turn loop natural finish → `Completed`/`Failed`. `finish` refuses with `run <id> is still executing` and hint `deadreckon attach …` (`main.rs:6845`). `apply` refuses with `run <id> is executing` and `deadreckon resume <id>` (`main.rs:7047`). `abandon` refuses without `--force` (`main.rs:7337`). `cleanup <id>` refuses without `--force` (`main.rs:7367`). |
| `Completed` | `completed` | `state: completed -> finish (apply)` / `-> finish (export)` / `-> finish (review)` depending on codebase mode (`main.rs:8722-8729`); cleanup-marker overrides as `done`, `abandoned`, `cleaned` (`main.rs:8713,8733`) | TUI footer/header reflects via `RunCompleted`; after-completion key-handling in `handle_tui_completion_key` (`main.rs:10219`) | `finish` routes to `apply`/`materialize`/in-place review (`main.rs:6862-6912`); `materialize` → adds `.materialized-to` marker; `apply` → writes `abandoned.json` with reason `applied` (`main.rs:7188/7533`); `abandon` → writes reason `abandoned`; `extend` requires Completed (`main.rs:7580-7585`); `doc --polish` requires Completed (`main.rs:8838`). |
| `Failed` | `failed` | `state: failed -> resume` (`main.rs:8721`); failure reason printed under `run health` `failure: …` (`main.rs:9704`) | TUI `footer_for_state` shows failure | `resume_command` clears `failure_reason`, sets `Planned`, runs (`main.rs:9208-9218`). `finish` refuses with `run <id> is failed` hint `deadreckon resume <id>` (`main.rs:6852`). |
| `Killed` | `killed` | `state: killed -> resume` (`main.rs:8721`); reason `killed by user` in `failure:` line | TUI footer | `resume_command` restarts; `cleanup --force` for stale executing→killed. Final write set in `kill_loaded_run` (`main.rs:9105-9153`) emits `RunCompleted{status:"killed"}`. |

Additional pseudo-states surfaced only via markers (no enum):
- **Abandoned** (`abandoned.json` reason `abandoned`) — `next_action_label` shows `abandoned`; `cleanup` skips re-cleaning these (`main.rs:7459`).
- **Applied** (`abandoned.json` reason `applied`) — `next_action_label` shows `done`; `cleanup_marker_reason` `main.rs:8742`.
- **Cleaned** (`abandoned.json` reason `cleaned`) — shows `cleaned` or `done`.
- **Promoted to library** (`promoted_library_dir` set) — `print_run_locations` adds `artifact …` and `note launch-dir is unchanged…` line (`main.rs:9786-9791`).
- **Polish failed** (DocsStatus::Failed) — printed in `print_status_card` `docs: polish failed (...); fallback docs are still available` (`main.rs:9710-9718`).
- **Stale executing** — `is_stale_executing` (`main.rs:9173-9187`): exec status with no living supervised pid, or no pids and >=5 min idle; surfaced as `cleanup --stale` next action (`main.rs:8716-8718`).

### Chain states (`ChainStatus`) — `crates/deadreckon-core/src/chain.rs:18-28`

| Enum variant | Stored text (`snake_case`) | CLI label (`chain_status_label`, `main.rs:3937-3947`) | Transitions out |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Pending` | `pending` | `pending` | `chain run`/`resume` → `Running`. |
| `Running` | `running` | `running` | `chain pause` → `Paused` (prints `paused <id>` + `try: deadreckon chain resume …`, `main.rs:3155-3159`). `chain kill` → `Killed` (`killed <id>`, `main.rs:3230`). Conductor naturally pauses on hook/preview/manual/cap (`pause_chain_at_step`, `main.rs:2540`); on completion → `Completed`. |
| `Paused` | `paused` | `paused` | `chain resume` (alias for `chain run` if id given, `main.rs:1509`); `chain extend` (`extended <id>`, `main.rs:3345`); `chain undo` (`undone <id>`); `chain redo` (`redo queued <id>`, `main.rs:3420`). |
| `Completed` | `completed` | `completed` | `chain extend --insert-at` flips it back to `Paused` with reason `extended` (`main.rs:3333-3335`); `chain undo` → `Undone`. `chain run/resume` refuses with `chain '<id>' is completed` hint `deadreckon chain show <id>` (`main.rs:1872`). |
| `Failed` | `failed` | `failed` | Same as Paused recovery commands. |
| `Killed` | `killed` | `killed` | `chain extend`/`undo`/`redo` (no explicit guard in those functions besides the `Completed` carve-out). |
| `Undone` | `undone` | `undone` | None enforced; user usually starts a new chain. |

### Chain step states (`ChainStepStatus`)
Stored snake_case: `pending|running|completed|failed|skipped|applied|undone`. Rendered identically by `chain_step_status_label` (`main.rs:3949-3958`). Glyphs (`chain_step_dot`): `○ ● ◐ ✗ ↷ ● ↶` — note `Running` and `Applied` share `●`.

### Phases (`PhaseStatus`) — `state.rs:47-67`
`Pending|Planned|Executing|Completed|Failed`. Printed by `print_status_card` as `phase: <id> <name>` (`main.rs:9655-9664`). The status-card never separately surfaces phase status text; only id+name. Phase 60 (`complete`) flips run to Completed (`state.rs:168`).
